﴿ومن أوفى بما عاهد عليه الله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; من: a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; أوفى: the protasis; بما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أوفى; the clause عاهد is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. عليه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عاهد; the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فسيؤتيه أجرًا عظيما﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis; يؤتيه: a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; أجرًا: a second mafʿūl bihi; عظيمًا: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿سيقول لك المخلفون من الأعراب شغلتنا أموالنا وأهلونا﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future; يقول: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); لك is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقول﴾; المخلفون: fāʿil (agent); من الأعراب: a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause شغلتنا أموالنا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); أهلونا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أموالنا, the sign of its nominative being the wāw, because it is treated as a sound masculine plural (mulḥaq bi-jamʿ al-mudhakkar al-sālim).
﴿فاستغفر لنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; استغفر: an imperative verb; لنا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to استغفر; the object of استغفر is omitted, i.e. the Name of Majesty الله.
﴿يقولون بألسنتهم ما ليس في قلوبهم﴾: the clause is the object of the saying of Allah the Exalted; يقولون: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; بألسنتهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يقولون; ما: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ليس: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), implied as "it"; في قلوبهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). The clause ﴿ليس في قلوبهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿قل فمن يملك لكم من الله شيئا إن أراد بكم ضرا أو أراد بكم نفعا﴾: قل: an imperative verb; the fāʾ is a conjunction; من: an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); يملك: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "he"; the clause is the khabar of من, and the [whole] clause is the object of قل; لكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يملك; من الله: a ḥāl; شيئًا: the object of يملك; إن: a conditional particle; أراد: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then who has power…"; بكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أراد; خيرًا: the object of أراد [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in this part of the ayah is ﴿ضرا﴾]; the clause أو أراد بكم نفعًا is conjoined to the preceding clause.
﴿بل كان الله بما تعملون خبيرا﴾: بل: a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī), moving from one topic to another; كان: a defective past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; بما: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خبيرًا﴾; the clause ﴿تعملون﴾ is the ṣila, with no grammatical position; خبيرًا: the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿بل﴾: also a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿ظننتم﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿أن﴾: أن is lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause ﴿لن يخرج...﴾ is its khabar (predicate) [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently carried over from Q 47:29; the clause here is ﴿لن ينقلب...﴾]; أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of ظننتم.
﴿لن﴾: a particle of negation, the accusative and the future.
﴿ينقلب﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن.
﴿الرسول﴾: fāʿil.
﴿والمؤمنون﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الرسول.
﴿إلى أهليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينقلب﴾.
﴿أبدًا﴾: an adverb, also attached to ﴿ينقلب﴾.
﴿وزين﴾: a passive past verb (built for an unnamed agent).
﴿ذلك﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿في قلوبكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿زين﴾.
﴿وظننتم﴾: conjoined to وزين.
﴿ظن﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿السوء﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وكنتم﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the tāʾ is its noun.
﴿قومًا﴾: its khabar.
﴿بورًا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قومًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿ومن لم يؤمن بالله ورسوله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, confirming their ruin; من: a jussive conditional noun, or a relative noun, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); لم: a particle of negation, of conversion [to past meaning] and of the jussive; يؤمن: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم; بالله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤمن﴾; رسوله is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الله; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "then he is a disbeliever".
﴿فإنا أعتدنا للكافرين سعيرا﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to the apodosis; إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿نا﴾: its noun; the clause أعتدنا is the khabar (predicate) of إن; للكافرين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعتدنا﴾; سعيرًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the conditional clause with its apodosis is the khabar of من if it is conditional, and the clause فإنا أعتدنا is the khabar if it is a relative noun, the fāʾ entering because of the sense of condition contained in the relative noun.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿ولله ملك السماوات والأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ملك السماوات والأرض: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يغفر is a ḥāl (circumstantial); لمن: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يغفر﴾; the clause يشاء is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ويعذب من يشاء is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause of the ṣila.
﴿وكان الله غفورا رحيما﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; غفورا: its first khabar; رحيمًا: its second khabar.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿سيقول المخلفون إذا انطلقتم إلى مغانم لتأخذوها ذرونا نتبعكم﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future; يقول المخلفون: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); إذا: a future adverb containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يقول; the clause انطلقتم is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the adverb's annexation to it; إلى مغانم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to انطلقتم; the clause ذرونا is the object of their saying, i.e. "let us"; نتبعكم: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab).
﴿يريدون أن يبدلوا كلام الله﴾: the clause يريدون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil, namely المخلفون, and you may make it resumptive, with no grammatical position; it has also been said: a ḥāl from the object pronoun in ﴿ذرونا﴾, but this is strained and far-fetched; أن and what follows it are the object of يريدون; كلام الله: the object of يبدلوا.
﴿قل لن تتبعونا كذلكم قال الله﴾: قل: an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; لن: a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; تتبعونا: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿لن﴾, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and نا is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿كذلكم﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a saying like this saying issuing from me"; ﴿ذلكم﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the lām is for distance, the kāf is a particle of address, and the mīm is for the plural; ﴿قال﴾: a past verb; the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil.
﴿من قبل﴾: من: a preposition; ﴿قبل﴾: an adverb of time, indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿قال﴾.
﴿فسيقولون بل تحسدوننا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; the sīn is a particle of the future; يقولون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); بل: a particle of digression (iḍrāb), or of conjunction; تحسدوننا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿سيقولون﴾; it is an imperfect verb, nominative, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿بل كانوا لا يفقهون﴾: بل: a second digression, away from describing them as attributing envy to the believers, to what is worse than that, namely ignorance; كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the wāw of the group is its noun; the clause لا يفقهون is its khabar (predicate).
﴿إلا قليلا﴾: إلا: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); قليلًا: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a little understanding".

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿قل﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you".
﴿للمخلفين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قل﴾.
﴿من الأعراب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ستدعون﴾: the clause ستدعون is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿إلى قوم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تدعون﴾.
﴿أولي بأس شديد﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قوم﴾.
﴿تقاتلونهم أو يسلمون﴾: the clause تقاتلونهم is a second naʿt, or a ḥāl, or resumptive, with no grammatical position; أو: a conjunction particle; يسلمون is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تقاتلونهم; and you may take the imperfect verb as nominative (marfūʿ) by way of resumption, the implied form being: أو هم يسلمون ("or they submit").
﴿فإن تطيعوا يؤتكم الله أجرا حسنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن: conditional; تطيعوا: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; يؤتكم: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الله: fāʿil; أجرًا: the second mafʿūl bihi; حسنًا: a naʿt of ﴿أجرًا﴾.
﴿وإن تتولوا كما توليتم من قبل يعذبكم عذابا أليما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن: conditional; تتولوا: the protasis; ﴿كما﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya (infinitival); ﴿توليتم﴾: a verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar from the maṣdariyya ﴿ما﴾ and the verb is muḍāf ilayhi; من قبل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to توليتم; قبل is indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording, not in meaning; يعذبكم: the apodosis; the kāf is its object; عذابا stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar); أليمًا: a naʿt of ﴿عذابًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج﴾: ليس: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; على الأعرج [Translator's note: so in the source; the first phrase after ليس is ﴿على الأعمى﴾]: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of ليس; حرج: its postponed noun; and what follows is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.
﴿ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; من: conditional, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); يطع الله ورسوله: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); يدخله: its apodosis (jawāb); جنات: a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is an adjective of ﴿جنات﴾.
﴿ومن يتول يعذبه عذابا أليما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من: conditional, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; يتول: the protasis; يعذبه: its apodosis; عذابا stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar); أليما: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عذابا﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿لقد رضي الله عن المؤمنين إذ يبايعونك تحت الشجرة﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); رضي الله: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); عن المؤمنين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رضي﴾; إذ: an adverb of past time, attached to ﴿رضي﴾; the clause يبايعونك is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi; تحت الشجرة: an adverb attached to ﴿يبايعونك﴾.
﴿فعلم ما في قلوبهم فأنزل السكينة عليهم وأثابهم فتحا قريبا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; علم: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "he", referring to Allah the Exalted; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يبايعونك, given what was said earlier, that it has the sense of the past; ما: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في قلوبهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. فأنزل is conjoined to فعلم; السكينة: mafʿūl bihi; أثابهم is also conjoined; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi; فتحًا: the second mafʿūl bihi; قريبًا: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿ومغانم كثيرة يأخذونها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; مغانم is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿فتحًا قريبًا﴾; the clause يأخذونها is an adjective of ﴿مغانم﴾.
﴿وكان الله عزيزا حكيما﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; عزيزًا: the first khabar (predicate) of كان; حكيمًا: the second khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl); يغفر: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فتحنا﴾; لك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يغفر﴾; الله: fāʿil (agent); ما: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿تقدم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. من ذنبك: a ḥāl (circumstantial); وما تأخر is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ما تقدم.
﴿ويتم نعمته عليك ويهديك صراطا مستقيما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يتم is conjoined to ليغفر; نعمته: mafʿūl bihi; عليك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نعمته or to يتم; يهديك is also conjoined; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi; صراطًا: the second mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition; مستقيمًا: a naʿt (adjective), accusative by the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وعدكم الله مغانم كثيرة تأخذونها﴾: وعدكم الله: a past verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a postponed fāʿil (agent); مغانم: a second mafʿūl bihi; كثيرة: an adjective; the clause تأخذونها is a second adjective.
﴿فعجل لكم هذه وكف أيدي الناس عنكم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; عجل: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), referring to Allah; لكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) عجل; هذه: mafʿūl bihi; وكف أيدي الناس عنكم is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes.
﴿ولتكون آية للمؤمنين ويهديكم صراطا مستقيما﴾: the wāw conjoins to something implied, i.e. "so that you may thank Him"; the noun of ﴿تكون﴾ is a latent pronoun, implied as "it" (hiya); آية: its khabar (predicate); للمؤمنين: a naʿt (adjective) of آية; يهديكم is conjoined to ولتكون; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi; صراطًا: the second mafʿūl bihi; مستقيمًا: an accusative naʿt of ﴿صراطا﴾.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿وأخرى لم تقدروا عليها قد أحاط الله بها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أخرى is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to هذه; it has also been said: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause لم تقدروا عليها being its adjective and the clause قد أحاط الله بها its khabar (predicate); and it has been said: ﴿أخرى﴾ is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb indicated by ﴿قد أحاط الله بها﴾, its implied form being: "وقضى الله أخرى قد أحاط بها" ("and Allah decreed another which He has encompassed"). And it has been said: it is genitive (majrūr) by an implied رُبّ, the wāw being the wāw of rubba, with ﴿لم تقدروا﴾ an adjective and ﴿قد أحاط﴾ the khabar.
﴿وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; قديرًا: its khabar; ﴿على كل شيء﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قديرًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿ولو قاتلكم الذين كفروا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; لو: conditional; قاتلكم: a verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذين: fāʿil (agent); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿لولوا﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; ولوا: a verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of لو.
﴿الأدبار﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿ولو قاتلكم الذين...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿ثم لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا﴾: ثم: a conjunction particle; لا: negative; يجدون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil; وليًّا: mafʿūl bihi; ولا نصيرًا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿سنة الله التي قد خلت من قبل﴾: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb from its own root, i.e. سنَّ الله ذلك سنة ("Allah established that as a practice"). The Name of Majesty: muḍāf ilayhi. التي: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سنة﴾. The clause ﴿قد خلت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position. من قبل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلت﴾; and the wāw is a conjunction.
﴿ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا﴾: لن: a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; تجد: an imperfect verb, accusative by ﴿لن﴾; لسنة الله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجد﴾; تبديلًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿وهو الذي كف أيديهم عنكم وأيديكم عنهم ببطن مكة من بعد أن أظفركم عليهم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿كَفَّ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. أيديهم: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عنكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كف; the clause ﴿وهو الذي...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; وأيديكم عنهم is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أيديهم عنكم; ببطن مكة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being in the valley of Mecca"; من بعد: a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to كف; أن with what falls within its scope is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation to the adverb; عليهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أظفركم﴾.
﴿وكان الله بما تعملون بصيرا﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; بصيرًا: its khabar; بما تعملون: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿بصيرًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿هم الذين كفروا وصدوكم عن المسجد الحرام والهدي معكوفا﴾: هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذين: its khabar (predicate); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; صدوكم is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila; عن المسجد: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) صدوكم; الحرام: a naʿt (adjective). الهدي is conjoined to the accusative pronoun in صدوكم, or it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), the wāw being for accompaniment (maʿiyya); معكوفًا: a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿أن يبلغ محله﴾: أن with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, accusative (manṣūb) by removal of the preposition, i.e. عن أن يبلغ or من أن يبلغ ("from reaching"), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to صدوكم or to ﴿معكوفًا﴾. Or the interpreted maṣdar is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), because it is the reason for the barring, the implied form being: "صدوا الهدي كراهة أن يبلغ محله" ("they barred the offering, disliking that it should reach its place"); or it is the reason for ﴿معكوفًا﴾. Some parsed it as a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from الهدي, i.e. "barring the offering's reaching its place".
﴿ولولا رجال مؤمنون ونساء مؤمنات لم تعلموهم أن تطئوهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لولا: a particle of non-occurrence due to existence (imtināʿ li-wujūd); رجال: a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "موجودون بمكة" ("present in Mecca"); مؤمنون: a naʿt of رجال; نساء مؤمنات is conjoined to ﴿رجال مؤمنون﴾; the clause لم تعلموهم is an adjective of the men and the women together; أن with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, a badal of inclusion from رجال and نساء, or from the attached pronoun in ﴿تعلموهم﴾.
﴿فتصيبكم منهم معرة بغير علم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; تصيبكم: an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to تطئوهم; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the mīm the sign of the plural; منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تصيبكم; معرة: the fāʿil (agent) of تصيبكم; بغير علم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the kāf, or to an omitted adjective of معرة.
﴿ليدخل الله في رحمته من يشاء﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl); يدخل: an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something implied, i.e. "the absence of [your being given] power over the people of Mecca came about [so that…]"; في رحمته: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يدخل; من يشاء: mafʿūl bihi; the clause يشاء is the ṣila, with no grammatical position.
﴿لو تزيلوا لعذبنا الذين كفروا منهم عذابا أليما﴾: لو: conditional; تزيلوا: a past verb and its fāʿil; the lām is the linking lām; the clause عذبنا has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of لو; عذبنا: a verb and its fāʿil; الذين كفروا: mafʿūl bihi; منهم: a ḥāl; عذابا stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar); أليمًا: an adjective.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿إذ جعل الذين كفروا في قلوبهم الحمية حمية الجاهلية﴾: ﴿إذ﴾: an adverb of past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عذبنا﴾ or to ﴿صدوكم﴾; or ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, implied as اذكر ("remember"); the clause ﴿جعل﴾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi; الذين: fāʿil (agent); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; في قلوبهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جعل if it means "cast", or to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of جعل if it means "made [to become]"; الحمية: the first mafʿūl bihi; حمية الجاهلية: a badal (substitute).
﴿فأنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وألزمهم كلمة التقوى﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to something implied that must be supplied, understood from the context; فأنزل الله: a verb and its fāʿil; سكينته: mafʿūl bihi; على رسوله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أنزل﴾; وعلى المؤمنين is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes; ألزمهم is also conjoined; the hāʾ is the first object; كلمة التقوى: the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وكانوا أحق بها وأهلها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿كانوا﴾: كان and its noun. أحق: the khabar (predicate) of كان. بها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أحق﴾. أهلها: conjoined to ﴿أحق﴾, accusative.
﴿وكان الله بكل شيء عليما﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; بكل شيء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عليمًا﴾; عليمًا: the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); صدق الله: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); رسوله: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الرؤيا: accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in his vision"; and it has been said: صدق takes two objects; بالحق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) صدق, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرؤيا.
﴿لتدخلن المسجد الحرام﴾: the lām: the answer to an omitted oath; تدخلن: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of a succession of identical letters, since it is one of the five verbs; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil; the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; المسجد: mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); الحرام: an adjective.
﴿إن شاء الله﴾: إن: conditional; ﴿شاء﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The Name of Majesty: fāʿil, nominative. The conditional clause ﴿إن شاء الله﴾ is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.
﴿آمنين محلقين رءوسكم ومقصرين لا تخافون﴾: آمنين: a ḥāl from the wāw dropped from ﴿لتدخلن﴾ because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, i.e. a ḥāl concurrent with the entering. محلقين: a second, overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl; رؤوسكم: mafʿūl bihi; لا: negative; تخافون: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or a ḥāl from the fāʿil of لتدخلن, or from the pronoun in آمنين, or in محلقين.
﴿فعلم ما لم تعلموا فجعل من دون ذلك فتحا قريبا﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to the clause صدق الله; علم: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; ما: mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿لم تعلموا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. فجعل: the fāʾ is a conjunction; من دون ذلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جعل; فتحًا: mafʿūl bihi; قريبًا: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿هو﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿الذي﴾: its khabar (predicate).
﴿أرسل رسوله﴾: the clause أرسل رسوله is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿بالهدى﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "clothed with guidance".
﴿ودين الحق﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الهدى.
﴿ليظهره﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl); يظهره: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أرسل.
﴿على الدين كله﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿أرسل﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; one would expect ﴿يظهره﴾]; كله: a tawkīd (emphasis) of الدين; the ﴿أل﴾ in الدين is generic (for the genus), meaning the various religions.
﴿وكفى بالله شهيدا﴾: كفى: a past verb; the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) particle; the Name of Majesty is genitive in wording and the fāʿil (agent) of كفى in position; شهيدًا: a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿محمد رسول الله﴾: محمد: mubtadaʾ (subject); رسول الله: its khabar (predicate).
﴿والذين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; الذين: a relative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ.
﴿معه﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿أشداء﴾: khabar.
﴿على الكفار﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أشداء﴾.
﴿رحماء﴾: a second khabar.
﴿بينهم﴾: an adverb attached to ﴿رحماء﴾.
﴿تراهم ركعا سجدا يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا﴾: the clause is a third khabar, and you may make it resumptive, with no grammatical position; تراهم: an imperfect verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), implied as "you"; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ركعًا and سجدًا: two ḥāls (circumstantials); the clause يبتغون is resumptive, with no grammatical position, as though it answered a question arising from their constancy in bowing and prostrating, as if it were said: "What do they seek by that?" and the reply were: "They seek…"; or it is a third ḥāl; فضلًا: mafʿūl bihi; من الله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يبتغون﴾; رضوانًا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿فضلا﴾.
﴿سيماهم﴾: mubtadaʾ.
﴿في وجوههم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar.
﴿من أثر السجود﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl.
﴿ذلك مثلهم﴾: ذلك: mubtadaʾ; مثلهم: its khabar.
﴿في التوراة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl.
﴿ومثلهم﴾: mubtadaʾ.
﴿في الإنجيل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl.
﴿كزرع﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as the khabar of مثلهم; ﴿زرع﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أخرج شطأه﴾: the clause is an adjective of زرع.
﴿فآزره فاستغلظ فاستوى﴾: conjoined to ﴿أخرج﴾, and likewise فاستغلظ.
﴿على سوقه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿استوى﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being upon its stalks, standing on them".
﴿يعجب الزراع ليغيظ بهم الكفار﴾: the clause is a ḥāl, i.e. "in its being pleasing"; الزراع: the object of يعجب; ليغيظ: the lām is causal (taʿlīl), and the imperfect verb is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a verb indicated by the context, i.e. "they were likened to that", so the cause is for the likening.
﴿وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات منهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما﴾: وعد: a past verb; الله: fāʿil; الذين: its object; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila, with no grammatical position; the clause عملوا الصالحات is conjoined to the ṣila; منهم: a ḥāl; مغفرة: a second mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition; أجرًا is conjoined to مغفرة; عظيمًا: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وينصرك الله نصرا عزيزا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes; نصرًا: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); عزيزًا: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿هو الذي أنزل السكينة﴾: هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿أنزل السكينة﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿في قلوب المؤمنين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزل﴾.
﴿ليزدادوا﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl); يزدادوا: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزل.
﴿إيمانًا مع إيمانهم﴾: a tamyīz (specification); مع: an adverb of place attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿إيمانًا﴾.
﴿ولله جنود السماوات والأرض﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لله: a fronted khabar; جنود السماوات والأرض: a postponed mubtadaʾ.
﴿وكان الله عليما حكيما﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; عليمًا: its first khabar; حكيمًا: its second khabar.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ليدخل المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl); يدخل: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted; المؤمنين: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يدخل; المؤمنات is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to المؤمنين; جنات: a second mafʿūl bihi of يدخل, by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is an adjective of جنات; خالدين فيها: a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ويكفر عنهم سيئاتهم﴾: conjoined to what precedes; سيئاتهم: the object of يكفر.
﴿وكان ذلك عند الله فوزا عظيما﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; ذلك: its noun; فوزًا: the khabar (predicate) of كان; عظيمًا: a naʿt (adjective); عند الله: an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of ﴿فوزًا﴾ and was fronted before it.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿ويعذب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يعذب: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يدخل; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), implied as "he".
﴿المنافقين﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿والمنافقات﴾: conjoined to المنافقين, accusative by the kasra, because it is a sound feminine plural.
﴿والمشركين والمشركات﴾: both conjoined to those two.
﴿الظانين﴾: الظانين: a naʿt (adjective), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿بالله﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾ a genitive (majrūr) noun, the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿الظانين﴾.
﴿ظن﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿السوء﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿عليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿دائرة السوء﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is one of supplication (duʿāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.
﴿وغضب الله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; غضب الله: a verb and its fāʿil.
﴿عليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿غضب﴾.
﴿ولعنهم﴾: also conjoined.
﴿وأعد لهم جهنم﴾: also conjoined.
﴿وساءت مصيرًا﴾: also conjoined; مصيرًا: a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ولله جنود السماوات والأرض﴾: the wāw is resumptive; لله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); جنود السماوات والأرض: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿ولله جنود..﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿وكان الله عزيزًا حكيمًا﴾: كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; عزيزًا: its first khabar; حكيمًا: its second khabar.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿نا﴾: its noun; the clause أرسلناك is its khabar (predicate); شاهدًا: a ḥāl (circumstantial); مبشرًا and نذيرًا are conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿شاهدًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿لتؤمنوا بالله ورسوله وتعزروه وتوقروه وتسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl); تؤمنوا: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسلناك﴾, because it is the reason for the sending; بالله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تؤمنوا﴾; رسوله is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty الله; تعزروه and what follows it are conjoined to ﴿تؤمنوا﴾, and the pronoun refers to the people; بكرة and أصيلًا are two adverbs of ﴿تسبحوه﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
The original is «إنّنا»; the nūn was dropped because of the accumulation of nūns. The nūn and alif in «إنّا» are in the position of an accusative, and in «فتحنا» in the position of a nominative; the markers of the pronoun often coincide when they are attached. The opening (al-fatḥ) here is the opening of al-Ḥudaybiya. Some people with no knowledge of the reports imagined that it is the conquest of Mecca. It is soundly established from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Barāʾ and Sahl ibn Ḥunayf that they said: it is the opening of al-Ḥudaybiya; and it is sound from Anas ibn Mālik, as was read out to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb [al-Nasāʾī], from ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī, who said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, saying: Qatāda narrated to us, from Anas ibn Mālik: إِنَّا فَتَحْنا لَكَ فَتْحاً مُبِيناً — he said: al-Ḥudaybiya. It is soundly established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said on his return from al-Ḥudaybiya: "A verse has been sent down to me that is dearer to me than this world and all that is in it," then he recited إِنَّا فَتَحْنا لَكَ فَتْحاً مُبِيناً (1) — the verse.
If it is said: The Prophet ﷺ did not love this world, so how did he say of this great and momentous favour that it is "dearer to me than this world"? The Arabs say this only of something exalted — they say, "He is more generous than Ḥātim of Ṭayyiʾ" — while this world has no worth; and the Prophet ﷺ said, when he passed by a dead sheep: "By Allah, this world is more insignificant to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than this is to its owners." There is more than one answer to that. Among them: that the meaning is "a verse has been sent down to me that is dearer to me than this world and all that is in it, if it were mine and I spent it in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic". It is also said: they were addressed with what they know.
«فتحا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and «مبينا» is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ: the lām of kay (purpose), and the meaning is "li-an" (in order that). Mujāhid said: ما تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ before prophethood, وَما تَأَخَّرَ after prophethood. Al-Shaʿbī said the like, except that he said: until he died. وَيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ: conjoined. It is said: He completes His blessing on him in this world by victory and in the Hereafter by reward. وَيَهْدِيَكَ صِراطاً مُسْتَقِيماً: it is said: the path of the Garden. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-ṣirāṭ is the clear course. Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied form is "to a path", then إلى was omitted [i.e. accusative by removal of the preposition].

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: وَيَنْصُرَكَ اللَّهُ: conjoined. نَصْراً عَزِيزاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun), and «عزيزا» is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-sakīna is mercy. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-sakīna is faʿīla from al-sukūn (stillness); and part of sakīna is forbearance, dignity, and leaving what does not concern one. Mālik ibn Anas narrated from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn — and some say: from al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with him — from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him." And regarding mercy is the ḥadīth that the Prophet ﷺ kissed al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, and al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis said to him: "I have ten children and I have never kissed any one of them." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy." In one ḥadīth: "What do you think, if Allah, Glorified be He, has removed mercy from your heart, what fault is it of mine?"
In [the transmission of] Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning لِيَزْدادُوا إِيماناً مَعَ إِيمانِهِمْ: he said: The Prophet ﷺ was sent with the testimony that there is no god but Allah, then He added prayer, then He added fasting, then He perfected their religion for them.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t:
لِيُدْخِلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ: two objects. خالِدِينَ: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَيُكَفِّرَ: conjoined; likewise وَيُعَذِّبَ الْمُنافِقِينَ وَالْمُنافِقاتِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَالْمُشْرِكاتِ. الظَّانِّينَ: a naʿt (adjective).
Mujāhid and Abū ʿAmr read «دائرة السُّوء» with ḍamma on the sīn. As for fatḥa on the sīn, even though reading with it is more common, ḍamma in this [expression] is, as al-Farrāʾ claimed, more common. al-sawʾ is the noun of the act, and al-sūʾ is the thing itself.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: An anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial of what is to be). [Translator's note: the word is not quoted in the source; it refers to شاهِداً وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً in إِنَّا أَرْسَلْناكَ شاهِداً وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً.]

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «ليؤمنوا» [with yāʾ], referring it back to هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ … ليؤمنوا. The reading with tāʾ is in the sense of "say to them"; and it is also said that addressing the Prophet ﷺ is addressing his community. وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ is for intensiveness; one [also] says ʿazarahu yaʿziruhu. Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «وتعزّروه», i.e. support him and honour him. وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ, i.e. glorify Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Qatāda said: «تعزّروه»: honour him; وَتُوَقِّرُوهُ: hold him as master and ennoble him. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd interpreted it as being for intensity; he said: from it comes "the ruler ʿazzara the man", i.e. went to great lengths in disciplining him, short of the prescribed penalty (ḥadd). Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān interpret it in the meaning of preventing; he said: "ʿazzartu the eminent man": I protected him and supported him; and "ʿazzartu the man": I beat him short of the ḥadd — its derivation being: I prevented him from returning to what I beat him for.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُبايِعُونَكَ: the noun of «إنّ». The khabar (predicate) may be إِنَّما يُبايِعُونَ اللَّهَ, and the khabar may be يَدُ اللَّهِ فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read وَمَنْ أَوْفى بِما عاهَدَ عَلَيْهُ اللَّهَ, bringing it according to the original. فسنؤتيه أجرا عظيما is permissible like the first; [one may also say] «فسنؤتيهو» with the wāw retained in connected speech, and «فسنؤتيهي» with the yāʾ retained in connected speech, the wāw being replaced by yāʾ. [Translator's note: the source prints the second form as «فسنؤتيه»; the description "retaining the wāw" requires «فسنؤتيهو».] Sībawayh and others reported all of this.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
سَيَقُولُ لَكَ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ: assimilation of the lām [into the lām of لك] is permissible even though it involves a meeting of two quiescents, because the first of them is a letter of prolongation and softness. Assimilation is not permissible in فَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَنا according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, because the rāʾ has repetition (takrīr), and if you assimilated it into the lām the repetition would be lost. يَقُولُونَ بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ: the plural [form] on the basis that lisān is masculine; whoever makes it feminine says alsun.
قُلْ فَمَنْ يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً إِنْ أَرادَ بِكُمْ ضَرًّا: this is the reading of most readers; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «ضُرًّا». [Translator's note: the source prints the majority reading with ḍamma (ضُرًّا) and the variant unvocalized; in the transmitted readings the majority read «ضَرًّا» and Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī «ضُرًّا».] A group of the specialists in rare words, among them Abū ʿUbayd, distinguished between them, saying: al-ḍarr is the opposite of benefit, and al-ḍurr is misery, as He said: أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 83]; on this basis al-ḍarr would have to be preferable here. But the grammarians reported that ḍarrahu ḍarran and ḍurran are both permissible, like shariba sharban and shurban.

nahhas-irab:12-14.t: وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْماً بُوراً: it is said that al-būr in the dialect of the Azd of ʿUmān is the corrupt. Al-Farrāʾ reported that al-būr in the speech of the Arabs is "nothing", and that one says "their deeds became būr", i.e. nothing.

nahhas-irab:15-16.t:
سَيَقُولُ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ إِذَا انْطَلَقْتُمْ إِلى مَغانِمَ لِتَأْخُذُوها ذَرُونا نَتَّبِعْكُمْ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُبَدِّلُوا كَلامَ اللَّهِ: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «كَلِمَ الله», the plural of kalima. Sībawayh's statement «هذا باب علم ما الكلم من العربيّة» intends by it the plural of kalima: he means three kinds of speech — noun, verb and particle. al-kalām is a generic noun. Some grammarians allowed al-kalām to have the meaning of al-taklīm (speaking to), and allowed "samiʿtu kalāma Zaydin ʿAmran" (I heard Zayd's speaking to ʿAmr). Abū Jaʿfar said: The true difference between al-kalām and al-taklīm is that kalām may be heard without the one who speaks it, whereas taklīm is heard only from the one who speaks it.
قُلْ لَنْ تَتَّبِعُونا كَذلِكُمْ قالَ اللَّهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ: that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: وَلَنْ تُقاتِلُوا مَعِيَ عَدُوًّا [al-Tawba: 83]. Then He, exalted be His praise, said after this: قُلْ لِلْمُخَلَّفِينَ مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ سَتُدْعَوْنَ إِلى قَوْمٍ أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ. It may be asked: how are they called to fighting when He said وَلَنْ تُقاتِلُوا مَعِيَ عَدُوًّا and rejected their saying ذَرُونا نَتَّبِعْكُمْ? The answer to this is that He said only لَنْ تُقاتِلُوا مَعِيَ عَدُوًّا, and these were not called in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; what shows you that is what comes after it: وَإِنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا كَما تَوَلَّيْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ. This answer is supported by the body of authority [holding] that Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on them, were the ones who called the Bedouins to fighting, as Ibn ʿAbbās said about His saying, Mighty and Majestic, سَتُدْعَوْنَ إِلى قَوْمٍ أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ: he said: to the Banū Ḥanīfa, the people of Musaylima; he said: and it is said: to Persia and Byzantium. Mujāhid and ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī said: إِلى قَوْمٍ أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ: Persia. Abū Jaʿfar said: So in this verse there is an indication of the imamate of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar and of their excellence, may Allah be pleased with them both, and that they took the imamate by right, because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: فَإِنْ تُطِيعُوا يُؤْتِكُمُ اللَّهُ أَجْراً حَسَناً; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would not give a good reward except to one who fought for the truth with a just imam.
Al-Kisāʾī said: تُقاتِلُونَهُمْ أَوْ يُسْلِمُونَ is by coordination. Abū Isḥāq said: «أو يسلمون» is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and the meaning is "or they will submit". Al-Kisāʾī said: In the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb it is «أو يسلموا», in the meaning "until they submit"; the Basrans say: in the meaning "ilā an" (until), as [the poet] said [metre: al-ṭawīl]:
428- أو نموت فنعذرا
(…or we die and so are excused.)

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: لَيْسَ عَلَى الْأَعْمى حَرَجٌ وَلا عَلَى الْأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلا عَلَى الْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ: the root meaning of ḥaraj in the language is narrowness. From Ibn ʿAbbās: this concerns jihād, and it was at the event of al-Ḥudaybiya, about those who stayed behind from it.

nahhas-irab:18-19.t: لَقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ: Jābir said: We were one thousand four hundred; we pledged allegiance on condition that we would not flee. وَأَثابَهُمْ فَتْحاً قَرِيباً: most of the people of exegesis hold that it is Khaybar, which was for the people of al-Ḥudaybiya; it is also said: it is the opening of al-Ḥudaybiya. Al-Zuhrī said: and it was a great opening.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: فَعَجَّلَ لَكُمْ هذِهِ: the people of exegesis hold that it is Khaybar. وَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَ النَّاسِ عَنْكُمْ: from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan, who said: it is ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn al-Fazārī and his people, and ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Naḍrī and those with him; they came to help the people of Khaybar while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was besieging them, and He cast terror into their hearts. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَلِتَكُونَ آيَةً لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ; it is said the meaning is: and that the spoils might be a sign, i.e. an indication of the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ and of his telling of the unseen.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَأُخْرى is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "and He promised you another". لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْها قَدْ أَحاطَ اللَّهُ بِها, i.e. He knew that it would come to be.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: وَلَوْ قاتَلَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوَلَّوُا الْأَدْبارَ: also from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan, that it concerns ʿUyayna and ʿAwf.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ: a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of لَوَلَّوُا الْأَدْبارَ is "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made that a practice (sanna)". Abū Isḥāq said: «سنّةُ الله» in the nominative is also permissible, i.e. "that is the practice of Allah".

nahhas-irab:24-25.t:
وَهُوَ الَّذِي كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ: several narrations have been reported about it. Among the best of them is that it was on the day of the conquest of Mecca: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, restrained the hands of the disbelievers by the terror He cast into their hearts, and restrained the hands of the believers by not commanding them to fight them. This is indicated by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ. مكة is a diptote because it is definite, the name of something feminine.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that He did not refrain from commanding them to fight them because they were believers; He informed that they are disbelievers, saying: هُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ. وَالْهَدْيَ is conjoined to the kāf and mīm, i.e. "and they barred the sacrificial animals". مَعْكُوفاً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ: «أن» is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "from reaching its place".
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made clear why He did not command them to fight them, saying: وَلَوْلا رِجالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ وَنِساءٌ مُؤْمِناتٌ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ أَنْ تَطَؤُهُمْ [Translator's note: so printed; the received text is «أَنْ تَطَئُوهُمْ»]: «أن» is in the position of a nominative as a badal (substitute), and the meaning is "were it not that you would trample them", i.e. kill them by trampling. And it is said: [the omitted apodosis is] "He would have permitted you to enter Mecca, but He came between you and that" لِيُدْخِلَ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ من أهل مكة بالوطء [of the people of Mecca, by the trampling]. [Translator's note: the words «بالوطء» at the end of this sentence appear out of place in the source; translated as written.] It is also said the meaning is that Allah, Glorified be He, knew that among these disbelievers were some who would embrace Islam and some to whom would be born those who would embrace Islam, so He did not command that they be killed; and it is said that it is on this basis that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade killing the People of the Book when they pay the jizya. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: لِيُدْخِلَ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ.
As for the meaning of فَتُصِيبَكُمْ مِنْهُمْ مَعَرَّةٌ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ: it is said: lest the Muslims be killed by mistake and blood-money be taken; and it is said: maʿarra, i.e. a blemish, so that it would be said: they were not God-fearing, since they killed the people of their own religion. Allah, Glorified be He, said: لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا لَعَذَّبْنَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً, i.e. had they been separated, We would have commanded you to punish them by killing.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
إِذْ جَعَلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ: it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: they are the polytheists who barred [them] from the Sacred Mosque and prevented the sacrificial animals from reaching their place. As for the true meaning of ḥamiyya in the language, it is disdain and refusal; if it is for what is due, it is good, and the one who shows it is called "protector of what must be guarded" (ḥāmī al-dhimār), as [the poet] said [metre: al-kāmil]:
429- حامي الذّمار على محافظة ... الجليّ أمين مغيّب الصّدر
(Protector of what must be guarded in safeguarding against the great calamity, trustworthy in what the breast conceals.)
If it is for what is not due, it is error and excess, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: حَمِيَّةَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ.
As for وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوى, the scholars have two views on it. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوى: "There is no god but Allah", and it is the head of all God-fearing. The same is narrated from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿUmar, Abū Hurayra and Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ, may Allah have mercy on them; they said: the word of God-fearing is "There is no god but Allah". Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated from al-Zuhrī, from al-Miswar and Marwān: وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوى — he said: meaning بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ. Al-Zuhrī said: When the document of the truce was written and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dictated (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم), they rejected that and said: "We know only 'In Your name, O Allah'"; so the Prophet ﷺ ordered that it be written as they said. These two views are not contradictory, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has bound the believers to the affirmation of [His] oneness and to «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم». They had also rejected in this document "From Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah", and said: "From Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh". [Translator's note: the source has «من محمد عبد الله»; «ابن» appears to have dropped out.] وَكانُوا أَحَقَّ بِها: [أحقّ is] the khabar (predicate) of كان, i.e. more entitled to it than others, because they are the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chose for him.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيا بِالْحَقِّ: then He explained the dream by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرامَ إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ. The scholars have discussed the meaning of «إن شاء الله» here, because an exception [of the will of Allah] does not occur in glad tidings so as to convey some benefit; the exception is only from created beings, because they do not know the outcomes of affairs. So it is said: the exception is from آمنين. It is also said: it only relates what was in the dream; and it is said: people were addressed with what they know. Among the good things said about it is that the exception is for those of them who would be killed or die. Some of the linguists claimed that the meaning is «لتدخلنّ المسجد الحرام إذ شاء الله» [Translator's note: the source prints «إن شاء الله», but the following refutation shows that «إذ» was meant], and claimed that it is like His saying وَذَرُوا ما بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ [al-Baqara: 278], and that its like is "and we, if Allah wills, will join you". This is a view not to be given any attention; none of the grammarians knows «إن» in the meaning of «إذ»; that is only «أن», so it is an error, and between them there is a distinction in the language and in the rulings, according to the jurists and the grammarians.
مُحَلِّقِينَ رُؤُسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «محلّقون رؤوسكم ومقصّرون» is permissible, in the meaning "some of you such and some of you such", and he recited [metre: al-basīṭ]:
430- وغودر البقل ملويّ ومحصود
(And the herbage was left, [some] twisted [and dried] and [some] harvested.)

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ: it is said: by proofs and demonstrations. It is also said: this must inevitably come to be. It is also said: it has already happened, because the Prophet ﷺ was sent when there were four religions, and all of them were overcome in his time and in the caliphate of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both. In [the transmission of] ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās, the meaning is: that He may make him prevail over (i.e. acquainted with) the whole matter of religion, i.e. that He may make it clear to him. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is among the best things said about the verse, because there is nothing that contradicts it.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ أَشِدَّاءُ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ: likewise. Qurra narrated from al-Ḥasan that he read وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ أَشِدَّاءُ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ رُحَماءُ بَيْنَهُمْ in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Translator's note: i.e. «أشدّاءَ … رحماءَ»; the source prints the received nominative vocalization], with the khabar of «الذين» being «تراهم»; and الذين may also be in the position of an accusative by an implied verb which تراهم explains. رُكَّعاً سُجَّداً: as a ḥāl. سِيماهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ مِنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ, i.e. their mark. The soundest thing said about it is that on the Day of Resurrection they will be recognized by the light in their faces; and in the ḥadīth: "My community will come with white blazes on their foreheads and white on their limbs."
ذلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ: mubtadaʾ and its khabar. فِي التَّوْراةِ completes the statement according to the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda, and مَثَلُهُمْ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ is then a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is كَزَرْعٍ. According to the view of Mujāhid the completion is at وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ — you conjoin one mathal to the other, then begin «كزرع», i.e. they are like a crop.
أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ: from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the ear, after being alone, puts forth with it seven ears or more. Ḥumayd narrated from Anas: أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ — he said: its growth and its offshoots. Abū Jaʿfar said: If you lighten the hamza, you say «شطه»: you throw its vowel onto the ṭāʾ and drop it. فَآزَرَهُ: the linguists said: i.e. it caught up with the mother plants; the root meaning of azarahu is "strengthened it". فَاسْتَغْلَظَ فَاسْتَوى عَلى سُوقِهِ: plural of sāq on the pattern fuʿūl, with something dropped from it. يُعْجِبُ الزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ الْكُفَّارَ: it is said: the kuffār here are the sowers, because they cover the seed; it is also said: they are those who disbelieved in Muḥammad ﷺ. This is more fitting, because it is not possible [to say] "it pleases the sowers, so that He may enrage the sowers by them".
وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ مِنْهُمْ مَغْفِرَةً وَأَجْراً عَظِيماً: «منهم» is better taken as specifying the genus (bayān al-jins), because if it were made partitive, the meaning of آمنوا would be "remained firm [in faith]", and that is figurative; a thing is not taken figuratively when its meaning is sound in the literal sense.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحاً مُّبِيناً﴾.
Qatāda related from Anas, who said: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحاً مُّبِيناً لِّيَغْفِرَ لَكَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِن ذَنبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ﴾ was revealed after the Prophet ﷺ returned from al-Ḥudaybiya. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than the whole world," then he recited it. A man of the Muslims said: May it bring you joy and ease! This is for you, O Messenger of Allah; so what is for us? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿لِيُدْخِلَ المُؤْمِنِينَ وَالمُؤْمِنَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الأَنْهَارُ﴾ to the end of the verse.
Mujāhid said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحاً مُّبِيناً﴾: We have decreed for you a clear decree.
Sufyān said: ﴿لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ﴾: that is, what was in the Jāhiliyya; ﴿وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ﴾: he said: what was in Islam, of what you have not yet done.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحاً مُّبِيناً﴾ there are three views close to one another:
a- Among them is what has preceded: that it is the opening of al-Ḥudaybiya. Al-Ḥudaybiya is a well after which the place was named.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And I know of no one among the lexicographers who doubles the yāʾ in it. In its opening there was the greatest of signs, because the Prophet ﷺ, according to what is related, came to this well when its water had been drained; so he ﷺ rinsed his mouth and spat into it, and the water came forth until everyone who was with him drank. And between them [and the idolaters] there was nothing but an exchange of shots, until the opening came. This is one view.
b- And it is said the meaning is: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحاً مُّبِيناً﴾ through avoiding the major sins, ﴿لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللهُ﴾ the minor sins.
c- And it is said: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحاً مُّبِيناً﴾ through guidance to Islam.
These views are close to one another, and Mujāhid's view combines them, because the opening of al-Ḥudaybiya is a decree among the decrees of Allah and a guidance among His guidance, by which He guides whom He wills; and likewise the avoidance of major sins.
And something that strengthens it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: I did not know what the meaning of ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا﴾ was until the daughter of Mishraḥ said to me: May Allah judge (fataḥa) between me and you.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالحَقِّ﴾.

nahhas-meani:2-3.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ وَيَهْدِيَكَ صِرَاطاً مُّسْتَقِيماً وَيَنصُرَكَ ٱللَّهُ نَصْراً عَزِيزاً﴾ [Verses 2 and 3].
That is, a help possessing might, with no abasement accompanying it.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ لِيَزْدَادُوۤاْ إِيمَاناً مَّعَ إِيمَانِهِمْ﴾.
﴿السَّكِينَةُ﴾: that is, calm and tranquillity.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً﴾.
That is, everything in them indicates that they have a Creator, and that He is One.

nahhas-meani:5-6.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِّيُدْخِلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ﴾.
That is, He opened for you through Islam and guidance by this.
And His saying, Glorified is He, also points to it: ﴿وَيُعَذِّبَ ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ وَٱلْمُنَافِقَاتِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَٱلْمُشْرِكَاتِ ٱلظَّآنِّينَ بِٱللَّهِ ظَنَّ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾.
Because they thought that the Prophet ﷺ would not return. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دَآئِرَةُ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾: that is, destruction.
And it is read: «السُّوْءُ»; and the difference between them is that «السَّوْءَ» is the thing itself, and «السُّوْءُ» is the act.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِداً وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, a witness over your community, ﴿وَمُبَشِّراً﴾ [bearing good tidings to] the doer of good among them, ﴿وَنَذِيراً﴾ [warning] the evildoer.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, and this is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, a circumstantial whose state comes about later).
Sībawayh reported: marartu bi-rajulin maʿahu ṣaqrun, ṣāʾidan bihi ghadan (I passed by a man with a falcon, [intending to be] hunting with it tomorrow).
So the meaning is: We have sent you, Our having decreed your witnessing on the Day of Resurrection. And on this basis you say: raʾaytu ʿAmran qāʾiman ghadan (I saw ʿAmr, [to be] standing tomorrow).

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِّتُؤْمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وَتُوَقِّرُوهُ وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلاً﴾.
Shuʿba related from Abū Bishr, from ʿIkrima, concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ﴾: he said: and fight alongside him with the sword.
Qatāda said: and help him.
And Juwaybir read: that is, and magnify him. «[Translator's note: the text has قرأ ("read"), though what follows is a gloss rather than a reading; قال ("said") seems intended.]»
And ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read ﴿وتَعْزُرُوهُ﴾.
Its origin in the language is from honouring and purifying; and from it is "al-taʿzīr", which is [a discretionary punishment] below the ḥadd (prescribed penalty).
And Muḥammad al-Yamānī read ﴿وَتُعَزِّزُوهُ﴾ with two dotted zāys. One says ʿazzazahu, i.e. he made him mighty and strengthened him; and from it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ﴾.
And it is possible that ﴿وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وَتُوَقِّرُوهُ﴾ refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, alone, and it is possible that it refers to the Prophet ﷺ.
As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلاً﴾,
it cannot be except for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He,
because its meaning must be either as Juwaybir said: and pray to Him;
or its meaning is: and glorify Him and declare Him free of imperfection.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ﴾.
That is, your contracting the pledge of allegiance with them is a contract for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَدُ ٱللَّهِ فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾.
That is, the hand of Allah in reward.
And it is said: in fulfilment.
And it is said: in His favour upon them through guidance.
﴿فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ in obedience.
﴿فَمَن نَّكَثَ فَإِنَّمَا يَنكُثُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ﴾: one says nakatha when someone breaks what he has bound himself to.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَيَقُولُ لَكَ ٱلْمُخَلَّفُونَ مِنَ ٱلأَعْرَابِ شَغَلَتْنَآ أَمْوَالُنَا وَأَهْلُونَا فَٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: They are the Bedouins of Medina, and Juhayna and Muzayna.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿شَغَلَتْنَآ أَمْوَالُنَا وَأَهْلُونَا﴾: that is, we have no one to guard our wealth and look after our families.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَيَقُولُ ٱلْمُخَلَّفُونَ إِذَا ٱنطَلَقْتُمْ إِلَىٰ مَغَانِمَ لِتَأْخُذُوهَا ذَرُونَا نَتَّبِعْكُمْ﴾ [Verse 15].
Mujāhid said: The Prophet ﷺ called them to go out to Mecca, but they refused and said: How can we go out with him to a people who came to him and killed his Companions? Then when the Prophet ﷺ went out, and seized a group off guard and sent them away, they said ﴿ذَرُونَا نَتَّبِعْكُمْ﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ أَن يُبَدِّلُواْ كَلاَمَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
And it is, according to the view of Ibn Zayd, His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقُلْ لَنْ تَخْرُجُوا
مَعِيَ أَبَداً وَلَنْ تُقَاتِلُوا مَعِي عَدُوّاً﴾.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُل لِّلْمُخَلَّفِينَ مِنَ ٱلأَعْرَابِ سَتُدْعَوْنَ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ أُوْلِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ تُقَاتِلُونَهُمْ أَوْ يُسْلِمُونَ﴾.
Sufyān related from Shuʿba, from Jaʿfar ibn Iyās, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr — Sufyān said: I think from Ibn ʿAbbās — ﴿سَتُدْعَوْنَ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ أُوْلِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾: he said: Hawāzin.
And ʿAṭāʾ said: They are Persia.
And al-Ḥasan said: Persia and Byzantium.
And among the soundest of what has been said about it is that they are "Banū Ḥanīfa", who were fought in the Ridda (apostasy wars); and this was among the things in the Qurʾān indicating the validity of the caliphate of Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.
And what shows you that is His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿تُقَاتِلُونَهُمْ أَوْ يُسْلِمُونَ﴾; so these are not among those from whom the jizya is taken.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوْاْ كَمَا تَوَلَّيْتُمْ مِّن قَبْلُ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ عَذَاباً أَلِيماً﴾.
That is, as you turned away [from going out] with the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
ʿUthmān ibn al-Mughīra said: I asked al-Ḥasan about His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ وَلاَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلاَ عَلَى ٱلْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ ﴾.
He said: This is concerning jihad.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّقَدْ رَضِيَ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ﴾.
Juwaybir said: They pledged allegiance on [the condition] that they would not flee.
And Qatāda said: They were one thousand four hundred, and the tree was a samura (acacia).
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَعَلِمَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَثَابَهُمْ فَتْحاً قَرِيباً﴾.
﴿فَعَلِمَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾: of sincerity.
﴿فَأنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: Qatāda said: patience and dignified composure.
﴿وَأَثَابَهُمْ فَتْحاً قَرِيباً﴾: Ibn Abī Laylā said: Khaybar.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَدَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً تَأْخُذُونَهَا فَعَجَّلَ لَكُمْ هَـٰذِهِ وَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنْكُمْ﴾.
His saying ﴿فَعَجَّلَ لَكُمْ هَـٰذِهِ﴾: Mujāhid said: He means Khaybar.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنْكُمْ﴾: because they had left their dependants behind, fearful for them; so Allah protected [them] from them, and restrained the hands of people from them.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأُخْرَىٰ لَمْ تَقْدِرُواْ عَلَيْهَا قَدْ أَحَاطَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيراً﴾.
Shuʿba related from Simāk al-Ḥanafī, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَأُخْرَىٰ لَمْ تَقْدِرُواْ عَلَيْهَا﴾: They are the conquests that have been opened for you.
And Ibn Abī Laylā said: They are Persia and Byzantium.
And Mujāhid said: It is whatever will come afterwards until the Day of Resurrection.
And Qatāda said: It is the conquest of Mecca.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ قَاتَلَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كفَرُواْ لَوَلَّوُاْ ٱلأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لاَ يَجِدُونَ وَلِيّاً وَلاَ نَصِيراً﴾.
Qatāda said: The disbelievers of Quraysh.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And if those of them who did not fight you had fought you, they would have been routed, because it is in the way (sunna) of Allah to help His allies.
Qatāda said — meaning concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿ثُمَّ لاَ يَجِدُونَ وَلِيّاً وَلاَ نَصِيراً﴾ —: and they will find for themselves no protector and no helper against Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُم بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ مِن بَعْدِ أَنْ أَظْفَرَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
He restrained the hands of the idolaters from those whom the believers had left behind when they went out to al-Ḥudaybiya.
Qatāda said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنكُمْ﴾: "A man from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ called "Zunaym" looked out [over the hill], and the idolaters shot him with an arrow and killed him. So the Prophet ﷺ sent out horsemen, and they captured twelve riders and brought them to the Prophet ﷺ. He said to them: Do you have a covenant or a guarantee of protection? They said: No. So he released them." Then Allah, Exalted is He, revealed ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُم بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ﴾.
Qatāda said: He means al-Ḥudaybiya.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ وَٱلْهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفاً أَن يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿وَٱلْهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفاً﴾: detained.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَن تَطَئُوهُمْ فَتُصِيبَكمْ مِّنْهُمْ مَّعَرَّةٌ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ لِّيُدْخِلَ ٱللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
﴿أَن تَطَئُوهُمْ﴾: that is, kill them; ﴿فَتُصِيبَكمْ مِّنْهُمْ مَّعَرَّةٌ﴾: that is, disgrace.
The idolaters would say: They killed the people of their own religion. And had you done so, Allah would [still] have admitted them into His mercy.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَوْ تَزَيَّلُواْ لَعَذَّبْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْهُمْ عَذَاباً أَلِيماً﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿لَعَذَّبْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾ by captivity and killing.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ كَلِمَةَ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn ʿUmar and Abū Hurayra said: ﴿كَلِمَةَ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾: There is no god but Allah.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَكَانُوۤاْ أَحَقَّ بِهَا وَأَهْلَهَا﴾.
That is, Allah chose them for His religion.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّقَدْ صَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ ٱلرُّءْيَا بِٱلْحَقِّ لَتَدْخُلُنَّ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ ٱلْحَرَامَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ لاَ تَخَافُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The Prophet ﷺ saw [in a dream] as though he and his Companions had entered Mecca with their heads shaved.
And Qatāda said: It is a dream the Prophet ﷺ saw at al-Ḥudaybiya, as though they had entered Mecca with their heads shaved and [hair] shortened; they found the dream slow [in coming true], then they entered after that.
As for His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾, there are several views on it:
a- Among them: that the meaning is: if I will, you shall enter in security.
b- And it is said: it is a report of what was said to the Prophet ﷺ.
c- And it is said: the servants were addressed according to what they ought to say, as the Exalted said ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذَلِكَ غَداً إلاَّ أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللهُ﴾.
d- And it is said: the exception (istithnāʾ) concerns those of them who would die or be killed.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَعَلِمَ مَا لَمْ تَعْلَمُواْ فَجَعَلَ مِن دُونِ ذَلِكَ فَتْحاً قَرِيباً﴾.
Mujāhid said: They returned from al-Ḥudaybiya, then Allah opened Khaybar to them.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُّحَمَّدٌ رَّسُولُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُ أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى ٱلْكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيْنَهُمْ تَرَاهُمْ رُكَّعاً سُجَّداً يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلاً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضْوَاناً سِيمَاهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلسُّجُودِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: That is the trace of the ablution water and the moist soil of the ground.
And ʿIkrima said: It is the trace of dust.
Ibn Wahb said: Mālik informed me concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿سِيمَاهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾: he said: It is what clings to the forehead of the dust of the ground. So this is one view.
And Mujāhid said: It is only humility and lowliness, and the hypocrite does not have this.
And al-Ḥasan said: A whiteness that will be on the face on the Day of Resurrection.
And ʿAṭiyya said: The place of the forehead will be whiter on the Day of Resurrection than the rest of the face.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: This is on the Day of Resurrection; their prayer will appear on their faces.
And Shimr ibn ʿAṭiyya said: It is the puffiness of the face and its paleness from staying awake at night.
And Qatāda said: They were described by prayer, i.e. they are known by prayer.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِي ٱلتَّوْرَاةِ وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي ٱلإِنجِيلِ كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿مَثَلُهُمْ﴾ means their description ﴿فى التوراة والإِنجيل﴾, i.e. written in them both.
And Qatāda said: What preceded is their likeness in the Torah, and they have another likeness in the Gospel, namely ﴿كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They are two likenesses: the first in the Torah and the second in the Gospel.
And Mujāhid said: They are a single likeness; and the complete stop (al-tamām), according to Mujāhid's view, is at ﴿فِي ٱلإِنجِيلِ﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ فَآزَرَهُ فَٱسْتَغْلَظَ فَٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِ﴾.
﴿كَزَرْعٍ﴾: that is, they are like a sown crop [Translator's note: i.e. khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject)].
﴿أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ﴾: Ḥumayd related from Anas, who said: its growth, its offshoots.
Abū ʿUbayda said: One says ashṭaʾa al-zarʿu when its offshoots come out.
Al-Farrāʾ said: The grain puts forth ten, seven or eight ears.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿فَآزَرَهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, it strengthened it and supported it.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They are the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ; they were few and became many, and were weak and became strong.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱسْتَغْلَظَ فَٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِ﴾.
[Sūq is] the plural of sāq (stalk). ﴿يُعْجِبُ ٱلزُّرَّاعَ﴾ is a similitude. ﴿لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ ٱلْكُفَّارَ﴾: Qatāda said: that is, so that Muḥammad ﷺ and his Companions may enrage the disbelievers.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ مِنْهُم مَّغْفِرَةً وَأَجْراً عَظِيماً﴾.
It is possible that "min" here is for explaining the genus (bayān al-jins), as the Exalted said: ﴿فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأَوْثَانِ﴾.
And it is possible that it is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), i.e. Allah has promised those of them who remained firm in faith forgiveness and a great reward.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
His saying: {لِّيَغْفِرَ لَكَ الله}: attached to «فَتَحْنا», and it is the lām of cause. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how was the conquest of Mecca made a cause of forgiveness? I say: it was not made a cause of forgiveness, but rather of the four things He enumerated, namely: forgiveness, the completion of favour, guidance to the straight path, and mighty help; as if He said: 'We made easy for you the conquest of Mecca and gave you victory over your enemy, so as to gather for you the glory of the two abodes and the aims of this life and the next.' It is also possible that the conquest of Mecca, inasmuch as it is jihād against the enemy, is a cause of forgiveness and reward." What he said contradicts the apparent sense of the verse, since the lām enters upon forgiveness, so forgiveness is the cause of the conquest and the conquest is given as caused by it; he ought therefore to have said: "How was the conquest of Mecca made to be caused by forgiveness?" and then to say: "It was not made so." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What is meant here is that Allah the Exalted opened [the way] for you so that He might make the conquest a sign of His forgiveness of you, so it is as if it were the lām of consequence (ṣayrūra)." This is speech that proceeds according to the apparent sense. Some said that this lām is the lām of oath and the original is «لَيَغْفِرَنَّ»; the lām was given kasra by likening it to the lām of purpose (lām kay) and the nūn was dropped. This is rejected: the lām is not given kasra, and it does not put the imperfect in the accusative. It might be said that this is not an accusative but the remains of the fatḥa that was before the nūn of emphasis, which remained to indicate it; but this is a rejected view.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {لِّيُدْخِلَ}: there are four views about what this lām is attached to. The first: something omitted, its implied form being: "He tests whomever He wills by these hosts, accepting good from those whom He has made fit for it, and evil from those for whom He decreed it, so that He may admit and punish." The second: that it is attached to His saying «إنَّا فَتَحْنا». The third: that it is attached to «يَنْصُرَك». The fourth: that it is attached to «يَزْدادوا». This was found problematic: His saying «ويُعَذِّبَ» is conjoined to it, and their increase in faith is not caused by Allah's punishing the disbelievers. It was answered: their belief that Allah punishes the disbelievers increases their faith without doubt. The Shaykh said: "And increase cannot be a cause of punishing the disbelievers." It was answered: it was mentioned because it is what the believer intends, as if it were said: "Because of your increase in faith He admits you to Paradise, and punishes the disbelievers by your hands in this world." There is room for doubt in this; he ought to have said: "It is not caused by the punishment of the disbelievers", and this resembles what preceded regarding {لِّيَغْفِرَ لَكَ الله} [al-Fatḥ: 2].
His saying: «عندَ الله»: attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl from «فوزاً», because it was originally its adjective. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be an adverbial of place, though there is disagreement about that, and also an adverbial for an omitted verb indicated by «الفوز», that is: "they succeed with Allah." It is not attached to «فَوْزاً», because it is a maṣdar, and its object does not precede it. Whoever tolerates that in the adverbial permits it.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {الظآنين بالله}: an adjective of the two groups. The disagreement about «السوء» was given in Sūrat al-Tawba. al-Ḥasan read «السُّوء» with ḍamma in both places.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {لِّتُؤْمِنُواْ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «ليؤمنوا» and what follows it with yāʾ (from below), going back to His saying «المؤمنين والمؤمنات». The others read with the tāʾ of address. al-Jaḥdarī read «تَعْزُرُوْه» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the zāy. He and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad likewise, except that they gave the zāy kasra. Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Yamānī read «ويُعَزِّرُوه» like the majority, except that it is with two zāys, from «العزَّة» (might). The accusative pronouns refer to Allah the Exalted. / It is also said: to the Messenger, except the last.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ الله}: the khabar of «إن الذين». And {يَدُ الله فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ} is a ḥāl clause, or a second khabar. It reinforces the figurative sense in pledging allegiance to Allah. Tamām ibn al-ʿAbbās read «يُبايعون الله». The object is omitted, that is: "They only pledge allegiance to you for Allah's sake."
His saying: «يَنْكُثُ»: Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يَنْكِثُ» with kasra on the kāf. The majority put the exalted name in the accusative. Ibn Abī Isḥāq put it in the nominative, meaning that the Exalted made a covenant with them. Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «فَسَنُؤْتيه» with the nūn of majesty. The others read with yāʾ (from below). «عَهِد عليه» was also read as a triliteral.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {شَغَلَتْنَآ}: al-Kisāʾī reported from Ibn Nūḥ that he read «شَغَّلَتْنا» with doubling.
His saying: «ضَرَّاً»: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read it with ḍamma on the ḍād. The others read it with fatḥa. It is said they are two dialectal forms with one meaning, like «الفُقْر» and «الفَقْر», «الضُّعْف» and «الضَّعْف». It is also said: with fatḥa it is the opposite of benefit, and with ḍamma it is a bad condition.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
