ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) read «إلى أهلِهم» without yāʾ, rather annexing «الأهل» in the singular. «وزَيَّنَ» was also read as an active verb, that is, Satan or your deed. And {كُنتُمْ قَوْماً بُوراً} means "you became". It is also said: on its usual sense of reporting that they were so in the past. «البُوْرُ» is destruction. It may here be a maṣdar used as a predicate for a plural, as in:
4077 - يا رسولَ الإِلهِ إنَّ لِساني ... راتِقٌ ما فَتَقْتُ إذ أنا بُوْرُ
(O Messenger of God, my tongue mends what I had torn when I was in ruin.)
Hence the singular and the masculine and their opposites are alike in it. It may also be the plural of «بائر», like «حُوْل» from «حائل» among the weak roots, and «بُزْل» from «بازِل» among the sound.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {وَمَن لَّمْ يُؤْمِن}: it may be conditional or relative. The overt noun stands in place of the returning pronoun on both views, that is: "then We have prepared for them."

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {يُرِيدُونَ}: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl from «المخلَّفون», or a ḥāl from the object of «ذَرُوْنا».
His saying: «كلامَ الله»: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «كَلِمَ», the plural of «كِلْمة». The others read «كلامَ». Abū Ḥaywa read «تَحْسِدُوْننا» with kasra on the sīn.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {أَوْ يُسْلِمُونَ}: the majority read it in the nominative, keeping the nūn, conjoined to «تُقاتلونهم» or as resumptive, that is: "or they will submit." Ubayy and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with the nūn dropped, putting it in the accusative by dropping it. The accusative is by an implied «أَنْ» according to the majority of the Basrans, and by «أو» itself according to al-Jarmī and al-Kisāʾī, and an interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a supposed maṣdar, as if it were said: "There will be fighting or submission." Similar in the accusative is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
4078 - فقلتُ له لا تَبْكِ عَيْنُك إنما ... نُحاول مُلْكاً أو نموتَ فَنُعْذَرا
(I said to him: "Do not weep; we are only seeking a kingdom, or we shall die and be excused.")
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«أو» has the meaning of «إلاَّ أَنْ» or «حتى»."

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ}: accusative by «رَضي». And «تحت الشجرة» may be attached to «يُبايعونك», or to something omitted as a ḥāl from the object. In the exegesis it is reported that he, peace be upon him, was sitting beneath it.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {وَمَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً}: that is: "and He gave you abundant spoils", or "He gave them spoils", or "He rewarded them with spoils", or "He rewarded you with spoils." I supplied second and third person because it is read «يَأْخُذونها» in the third person, which is the majority reading, and «تَأْخُذونها» in the second person, which is the reading of al-Aʿmash, Ṭalḥa and Nāfiʿ in the transmission of Saqlāb.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {وَلِتَكُونَ}: three views are permissible. The first: that it is attached to a verb implied after it, its implied form being: "and so that it might be, He did that." The second: that it is conjoined to an omitted cause, its implied form being: "He promised, and hastened [it], and restrained [their hands] so that you might benefit and so that it might be", or "so that you might give thanks and so that it might be." The third: that the wāw is redundant and the purpose clause relates to what precedes it, that is: "and He restrained so that it might be."

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {وأخرى}: several views are permissible. The first: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with {لَمْ تَقْدِرُواْ عَلَيْهَا} as its adjective and {قَدْ أَحَاطَ الله بِهَا} as its khabar. The second: that the khabar is omitted, implied before it, that is: "and there is another which you were not able to take." The third: that it is accusative by an implied verb under the condition of explanation, so the verb is supplied from the meaning of the later [clause], namely «قد أحاط الله بها», that is: "and Allah decreed another." 
The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied verb not under the condition of explanation, but because the context indicates it, that is: "and He promised another", or "and He gave you another." The fifth: that it is genitive by an implied «رُبَّ», the wāw being the wāw of «رُبَّ»; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it. In the noun in the genitive after the mentioned wāw there is a well-known disagreement: is it by an implied «رُبَّ» or by the wāw itself? But the Shaykh said: "«رُبَّ» does not occur as a governing preposition in the Qurʾān despite its frequent occurrence", meaning governing in the pronounced form; otherwise it is said that it governs in the implied form here and in His saying «رُبَما», on our view that «ما» is an indefinite described noun.
His saying: {قَدْ أَحَاطَ الله بِهَا} / may be the khabar of «أُخْرى» as above, or a second adjective if «أُخْرى» is said to be a mubtadaʾ with an implied khabar, or a ḥāl also.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {سُنَّةَ الله}: a maṣdar of emphasis for the content of the preceding sentence, that is: "Allah established that as a custom."

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ}: Abū ʿAmr read «يَعْلمون» with yāʾ (from below), going back to the third person in «أيديهم» and «عنهم»; the others read the second person, going back to the address in His saying «أيديكم» and «عنكم».

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {والهدي}: the majority put it in the accusative. The well-known view is that it is a conjunction on the accusative pronoun in «صَدُّوْكم». It is also said: accusative as accompaniment (maʿiyya); this is weak, since conjunction is possible. Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read it in the genitive, conjoined to «المسجد الحرام», and a muḍāf must be omitted, that is: "and from the slaughter of the offering." It was also read in the nominative, by an implied passive verb, that is: "and the offering was barred." The majority read it with fatḥa on the hāʾ and sukūn on the dāl; from Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and others it is reported with kasra on the dāl and the yāʾ doubled. Ibn Khālawayh reported three dialectal forms: «الهَدْيُ», which is the famous one and the dialect of Quraysh, «الهَدِيُّ» and «الهَدَى».
His saying: «مَعْكوفاً»: a ḥāl from «الهدي», that is: "held back"; one says «عَكَفْتُ الرجلَ عن حاجتِه». al-Fārisī denied that «عَكَفَ» is transitive by itself, while Ibn Sīda, al-Azharī and others affirmed it, and this is the apparent sense of the Qurʾān, given that a passive participle is formed from it.
His saying: «أَنْ يَبْلُغَ»: several views. The first: that it is by removal of the preposition, that is: «عَنْ أَنْ» or «مِنْ أَنْ». In that case this implied preposition may be attached to «صَدُّوكم» or to «معكوفاً», that is: "held back from reaching its place" in either wording. The second: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and then it may be the cause of the barring, the implied form being: "they barred the offering out of dislike that it reach its place"; or the cause of «معكوفاً», that is: "so that it might reach its place", with the holding back being by the Muslims. The third: that it is a badal ishtimāl from «الهَدْي», that is: "they barred the reaching of the offering to its place."
His saying: «لم تَعْلَموهم»: an adjective of the two kinds, with the masculine given precedence.
His saying: «أَنْ تَطَؤُوْهم»: may be a badal from «رجال» and «نساء», with the masculine given precedence as before, or a badal from the object of «تَعْلَموهم». The implied form on the first is: "and but for the trampling of unknown men and women", and on the second: "you did not know their trampling"; the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "and but for the presence of believing men and women who are existing or at hand". As for the apodosis of «لولا», there are three views. The first: that it is omitted, as the apodosis of «لو» indicates it. The second: that it is mentioned, namely «لَعَذَّبْنا», and the apodosis of «لو» is the omitted one, so he omitted from the first because of the second and from the second because of the first. The third: that «لَعَذَّبْنا» is the apodosis of both together, which is remote if he means that literally. al-Zamakhsharī said something close to this, for he said: "«لو تَزَيَّلوا» may be like a repetition of {لَوْلاَ رِجَالٌ مُّؤْمِنُونَ} since they return to a single meaning, and «لَعَذَّبْنا» would be the apodosis." The Shaykh denied that they return to a single meaning, saying: "because what the first is attached to is other than what the second is attached to."
His saying: «فتُصيبَكم»: conjoined to «أَنْ تَطَؤُوهم». Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn ʿAwn read «لو تَزايَلوا» on the pattern «تفاعَلوا».
The pronoun in «تَزَيَّلوا» may refer to the believers only, or the disbelievers, or both groups, that is: "had these been distinguished from those, We would have punished."
«الوَطْءُ» here is an expression for killing and trampling. He, peace be upon him, said: "O Allah, press Your tread hard upon Muḍar", and they recited: 4079 - ووَطِئْتَنا وَطْئاً على حَنَق ... وَطْءَ المقيَّدِ ثابِتَ الهَرْمِ
(You trampled us in rage, the trampling of a shackled man, firm on the Harm.)
«المَعَرَّة» is sin.
His saying: «بغيرِ عِلْمٍ»: may be attached to something omitted as an adjective of «مَعَرَّةٍ», or a ḥāl from the object of «تُصيبكم». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "from the genitive pronoun," meaning in «منهم», but his meaning is not apparent; or it may be attached to «يُصيبكم», or attached to «تَطَؤُوْهم».
His saying: «لِيُدْخِلَ اللَّهُ»: attached to something implied, that is: "the withholding of power over the people of Mecca and the withholding of punishment was so that Allah might admit."

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {إِذْ جَعَلَ}: the operator in the adverbial is either «لَعَذَّبْنا», or «صَدُّوكم», or "remember", in which case it is a direct object.
His saying: «في قلوبهم»: may be attached to «جَعَلَ», where it means "cast", and so takes one object, that is: "when the disbelievers cast zealotry into their hearts"; or attached to something omitted as a second object that was fronted, where it means "made".
His saying: «حَمِيَّةَ الجاهليةِ»: a badal from the preceding «الحميةَ». «الحميَّةُ» is disdain at something. It was recited for al-Mutalammis:
4080 - ألا إنني منهمْ وعِرْضي عِرْضُهُمْ ... كذا الرأسُ يَحْمي أنفَه أَنْ يُهَشَّما
(Indeed I am of them and my honour is their honour; thus the head protects its nose from being smashed.)
It means prevention. Its pattern is «فعيلة», and it is a maṣdar; one says «حَمَيْتُ عن كذا حَمِيَّةً».
His saying: «وكانوا أحَقَّ»: the pronoun may refer to the believers, which is the apparent sense, that is: "more entitled to the word of God-fearing than the disbelievers." It is also said that it refers to the disbelievers / that is: "Quraysh would have been more entitled to it, had it not been for their deprivation."

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {لَّقَدْ صَدَقَ}: «صَدَقَ» takes two objects, the second with a preposition; one says «صَدَقْتُكَ في كذا». It may be omitted, as in this verse.
His saying: «بالحَقِّ»: several views. The first: that it is attached to «صدق». The second: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "a truthfulness joined with the truth." The third: that it is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl from «الرؤيا», that is: "joined with the truth." The fourth: that it is an oath and its answer is «لَتَدْخُلُنَّ»; on this one pauses at «الرؤيا» and begins with what follows.
His saying: «لَتَدْخُلُنَّ»: the answer to an implied oath, or to His saying «بالحق» on that view. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«لَتَدْخُلُنَّ» is an explanation of the vision or resumptive, that is: 'By Allah, you will enter'", thus making its being the answer to an oath a counterpart to its being an explanation of the vision. This is not sound at all, namely that it be an explanation of the vision and not the answer to an oath; unless he means that it is the answer to an oath, but that it may be, together with the oath, an explanation, and that it may be resumptive and not an explanation, which is far from his wording.
His saying: «آمِنين»: a ḥāl from the agent of «لَتَدْخُلُنَّ», and likewise «مُحَلِّقين ومُقَصِّرِين»; «مُحَلِّقين» may also be a ḥāl from «آمِنين», so they would be nested.
His saying: «لا تَخافون»: it may be resumptive, or a third ḥāl, or a ḥāl either from the agent of «لَتَدْخُلُنَّ» or from the pronoun of «آمنين», «مُحَلِّقين» or «مقصِّرين». If it is a ḥāl from «آمِنين» or from the agent of «لَتَدْخُلُنَّ», it is a ḥāl of emphasis, and «آمنين» is a concurrent ḥāl, while what follows it is an anticipated ḥāl, except His saying «لا تَخافون» if it is made a ḥāl, for it is concurrent as well.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {مُّحَمَّدٌ رَّسُولُ الله}: it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, because when {هُوَ الذي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ} preceded, it indicated that implied element, that is: "He, that is, the one sent with guidance, is Muḥammad", and «رسولُ» is a badal, an explicative apposition or an adjective; or it may be a mubtadaʾ or a khabar; or it may be a mubtadaʾ with «رسولُ اللَّهِ» as the badal, explicative apposition or adjective as above. And «الذين معه» is conjoined to «محمدٌ», and the khabar about them is His saying {أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى الكفار}. Ibn ʿĀmir, in one transmission, read «رسولَ الله» in the accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ (specification), which supports its being a follower and not a khabar in the nominative case. On this view «والذين» may be genitive, conjoined to the exalted name, that is: "and the messenger of those who believed with him"; for when he was sent to them he was annexed to them, so he is the messenger of Allah in the sense that Allah sent him, and the messenger of his community in the sense that he was sent to them; and «أشدَّاءُ» is then the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "they are severe." It is also possible that the sentence is complete at «رسولُ الله» and «الذين معه» is a mubtadaʾ and «أشدَّاءُ» its khabar.
al-Ḥasan read «أشداءَ، رحماءَ» in the accusative: either for praise, or as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «معه», since it occurs as a ṣila, and the khabar is then about the mubtadaʾ.
His saying: {تَرَاهُمْ رُكَّعاً سُجَّداً}: two ḥāls, because the seeing is with the eye; likewise «يَبْتَغُون» may be resumptive, and if it is a ḥāl it may be a third ḥāl from the object of «تَراهم», or from the latent pronoun in «رُكَّعاً سجداً». Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed «سُجَّداً» to be an anticipated ḥāl from the pronoun in «رُكَّعاً». On this «يَبْتَغون» would be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «سُجَّداً», so it would be a ḥāl from a ḥāl, and that first ḥāl a ḥāl from another ḥāl.
Ibn Yaʿmar read «أَشِدَّا» with the short vowel, and the shortening is among the poetic licences, as in the saying:
4081 - لا بدَّ مِنْ صَنْعا وإنْ طالَ السَّفرْ ...
(There is no escape from Ṣanʿāʾ, even if the journey is long...)
Hence it is anomalous. The Shaykh said: "ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «ورُضوانا» with ḍamma on the rāʾ." I say: this is a mutawātir reading, read by ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Abū Bakr from him; I presented it in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, and excepted one word for him, namely the second in al-Māʾida.
«سِيْمِياؤهم» was also read with yāʾ after the mīm and a long vowel, which is an eloquent dialectal form, and it was recited:
4082 - غلامٌ رَماه اللَّهُ بالحُسْن يافعاً ... له سِيْمِياءُ لا تَشُقُّ على البصَرْ
(A youth whom God struck with beauty when still growing; he has a mark that does not strain the eye.)
The discussion of it and its derivation was given at the end of al-Baqara. And «في وجوههِم» is the khabar of «سِيماهم».
His saying: {مِّنْ أَثَرِ السجود}: a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its noun, which is «في وجوههم».
The majority read «مِنْ أَثَرِ» with two fatḥas; Ibn Hurmuz with kasra and sukūn; Qatāda «مِنْ آثارَ» in the plural.
His saying: «ذلك مَثَلُهم»: «ذلك» points to the preceding description of them as severe and merciful, with a mark on their faces. It is a mubtadaʾ with «مَثَلُهم» as its khabar, and «في التوراة» is a ḥāl from «مَثَلُهم», the operator being the sense of pointing.
His saying: {وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي الإنجيل}: two views are permissible. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «كزَرْعٍ», so one pauses at His saying «في التوراة», and they are two likenesses. To this Ibn ʿAbbās went. The second: that it is conjoined to the first «مَثَلُهم», so it is a single likeness / in both scriptures, and one then pauses at «الإنجيل». Mujāhid and al-Farrāʾ leaned to this. On this His saying «كزَرْع» has several views. The first: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "Their likeness is like a crop", explaining by it the likeness mentioned. The second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مَثَلُهم», that is: "resembling a crop whose description is this." The third: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "a likening like a crop"; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is not that. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ذلك» may be an obscure pointing made clear by His saying «كَزَرْع», as in His saying: {وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ الأمر أَنَّ دَابِرَ}."
His saying: «أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَه»: an adjective of «زرع». Ibn Kathīr and Ibn Dhakwān read it with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ; the others with sukūn. They are two dialectal forms. There are other dialectal forms of the word, read as anomalous: Abū Ḥaywa read «شَطاءَه» with the long vowel; Zayd ibn ʿAlī «شَطاه» with a clear alif after the ṭāʾ. This allows that it be a substitute for the hamza after transferring its vowel to the quiescent letter before it, in the dialect of those who say «المَراةُ» and «الكَماةُ» after the transfer, which is regular according to the Kufans; and it allows that it be a shortening of the lengthened form. Abū Jaʿfar and Nāfiʿ, in one transmission, read «شَطَه» with transfer and omission, which is the regular form. al-Jaḥdarī read «شَطْوَه», replacing the hamza with wāw, if it is an independent dialectal form. All these are dialectal forms for the shoots of a crop. One says «شَطَأَ الزَّرْعُ» and «أَشْطَأ», that is, it put forth its shoots. Is that confined to wheat only, or to it and barley only, or not confined? There is a well-known disagreement. He said:
4083 - أَخْرج الشَّطْءَ على وجهِ الثَّرى ... ومنَ الأشجارِ أفنانَ الثمرْ
(He brought forth the shoot upon the face of the soil, and from the trees the branches of fruit.)
His saying: «فآزَرَه»: the majority read it with the long vowel, on the pattern «أَفْعَل». They declared mistaken those who said it is «فاعَلَ», like Mujāhid and others, because «يُؤَازِرُ» was not heard as its imperfect, but «يُؤْزِرُ». Ibn Dhakwān read «فَأَزَره» with the short vowel, making it triliteral. «فأَزَّرَه» with doubling was also read. The meaning in all is: He strengthened it. 
It is also said: He made it equal. And it was recited:
4084 - بمَحْنِيَةٍ قد آزَرَ الضالُّ نَبْتَها ... مَجَرَّ جُيُوشٍ غانِميْنَ وخُيَّبِ
(In a bend of the valley, where the lote-tree strengthened its growth, the trail of armies, those who gained and those who were disappointed.)
His saying: «على سُوْقِه»: attached to «اسْتوى», and it may be a ḥāl, that is: "standing upon them." It was already mentioned in al-Naml that Qunbul reads «سُؤْقِه» with a quiescent hamza, as in his saying:
4085 - أحَبُّ المُؤْقِدين إليَّ موسى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The most beloved of the kindlers to me is Mūsā...)
and with a hamza with ḍamma followed by wāw like «قُرُوْح», together with the justification of that. «السُّوْق» is the plural of «ساق».
His saying: «يُعْجِبُ الزُّرَّاعَ»: a ḥāl, that is: "pleasing", and here the likeness ends.
His saying: «ليَغيظَ»: several views. The first: that it is attached to «وَعَدَ», because the disbelievers, when they hear of the believers' glory in this world and what is prepared for them in the Hereafter, are enraged by it. The second: that it is attached to something omitted, indicated by their likening to a crop in their growth and strengthening; said by al-Zamakhsharī, that is: "Allah likened them to that so that He might enrage." The third: that it is attached to what His saying {أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى الكفار} to the end indicates, that is: "He made them with these qualities so that He might enrage."
His saying: «مِنْهم»: this «مِنْ» is explicative, not partitive, because all of them are so; it is like His saying {فاجتنبوا الرجس مِنَ الأوثان} [al-Ḥajj: 30]. al-Ṭabarī said: "«منهم» means from the shoot which the crop put forth, and they are those who enter Islam until the Day of Resurrection", so he returned the pronoun to the meaning of «الشَّطْء», not its wording, and this is a good meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ اللَّهَ يَدُ اللَّهِ فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ فَمَنْ نَكَثَ فَإِنَّمَا يَنْكُثُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ أَوْفَى بِمَا عَاهَدَ عَلَيْهُ اللَّهَ فَسَيُؤْتِيهِ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ اللَّهَ) is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ. And (يَدُ اللَّهِ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it is the khabar; and the clause is another khabar of إِنَّ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «يُبَايِعُونَ», or resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَيَقُولُ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ إِذَا انْطَلَقْتُمْ إِلَى مَغَانِمَ لِتَأْخُذُوهَا ذَرُونَا نَتَّبِعْكُمْ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُبَدِّلُوا كَلَامَ اللَّهِ قُلْ لَنْ تَتَّبِعُونَا كَذَلِكُمْ قَالَ اللَّهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَسَيَقُولُونَ بَلْ تَحْسُدُونَنَا بَلْ كَانُوا لَا يَفْقَهُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُرِيدُونَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun in «ذَرُونَا».
It may also be a ḥāl from «الْمُخَلَّفُونَ», or resumptive. And (كَلَامَ اللَّهِ) with the alif. It is also read «كَلِمَ اللَّهِ», and the meaning is close.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ لِلْمُخَلَّفِينَ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ سَتُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى قَوْمٍ أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ تُقَاتِلُونَهُمْ أَوْ يُسْلِمُونَ فَإِنْ تُطِيعُوا يُؤْتِكُمُ اللَّهُ أَجْرًا حَسَنًا وَإِنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا كَمَا تَوَلَّيْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تُقَاتِلُونَهُمْ) may be resumptive, or a ḥāl muqaddara (anticipated circumstantial).
(أَوْ يُسْلِمُونَ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «تُقَاتِلُونَهُمْ». In some readings it is «أَوْ يُسْلِمُوا», and its position is accusative; «أَوْ» then means «إِلَى أَنْ» ("until"), or حَتَّى.

ukberi-tibyan:18-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ فَعَلِمَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَثَابَهُمْ فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا (١٨) وَمَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً يَأْخُذُونَهَا وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَغَانِمَ), i.e. "and He rewarded them with spoils", or "He rewarded you with spoils", because «تَأْخُذُونَهَا» is read both with tāʾ and with yāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:21-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأُخْرَى لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهَا قَدْ أَحَاطَ اللَّهُ بِهَا وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرًا (٢١) وَلَوْ قَاتَلَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوَلَّوُا الْأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا (٢٢) سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأُخْرَى), i.e. "and He promised you another", or "He rewarded you with another".
It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا» as its adjective (ṣifa) and «قَدْ أَحَاطَ» as the khabar (predicate).
It may also be that «هَذِهِ» [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently meaning the clause قَدْ أَحَاطَ] is an adjective, and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "and there is another". And (سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ) has been discussed in Subḥān [Translator's note: i.e. Sūrat al-Isrāʾ].

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَالْهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفًا أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ وَلَوْلَا رِجَالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ وَنِسَاءٌ مُؤْمِنَاتٌ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ أَنْ تَطَئُوهُمْ فَتُصِيبَكُمْ مِنْهُمْ مَعَرَّةٌ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ لِيُدْخِلَ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا لَعَذَّبْنَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْهَدْيَ): it is conjoined (maʿṭūf), i.e. "and they barred the sacrificial animals". And (مَعْكُوفًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْهَدْي. And (أَنْ يَبْلُغَ) is on the implied wording "from reaching" (مِنْ أَنْ يَبْلُغَ or عَنْ أَنْ يَبْلُغَ).
It may also be a badal (substitute) for الْهَدْي, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), i.e. "they barred the reaching of the sacrificial animals".
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَطَؤُهُمْ): it is in the position of the nominative as a badal of inclusion for «رِجَالٌ», i.e. "the trampling of men by killing".
It may also be a badal for the object pronoun in «تَعْلَمُوهُمْ», i.e. "you did not know them, (i.e.) your trampling them"; so it too is (a badal of) inclusion, and لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ is an adjective (ṣifa) of what precedes it. (فَتُصِيبَكُمْ) is conjoined to «تَطَؤُوا». And «بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ» is a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun, or an adjective of مَعَرَّة.
(لَعَذَّبْنَا) is the apodosis (jawāb) of لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا, and the apodosis of لَوْلَا is omitted, the apodosis of لَوْ making it unnecessary.
It is said that it is the apodosis of both together.
It is also said that it is the apodosis of the first, and the apodosis of the second is omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ جَعَلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوَى وَكَانُوا أَحَقَّ بِهَا وَأَهْلَهَا وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَمِيَّةَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ) is a badal (substitute); it is good because it was annexed to something that yields a meaning, so it is like the adjective of an indefinite noun used as a badal.
And (كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوَى), i.e. the practice (of it), or the uttering (of it), or the belief (in it); this was omitted because the meaning is understood.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيَا بِالْحَقِّ لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ لَا تَخَافُونَ فَعَلِمَ مَا لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا فَجَعَلَ مِنْ دُونِ ذَلِكَ فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا (٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالْحَقِّ) may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to صَدَقَ, or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرُّؤْيَا.
(لَتَدْخُلُنَّ) is the explanation of the vision; or it is resumptive, i.e. "by Allah, you will surely enter". And (آمِنِينَ) is a ḥāl, and the conditional is a fitting (musaddad) parenthesis. And (مُحَلِّقِينَ) is another ḥāl, or (a ḥāl) from the pronoun in آمِنِينَ. (لَا تَخَافُونَ) may be an emphasising ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), or resumptive, i.e. "you will never fear".

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا (٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالْهُدَى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "He sent him as a guide".

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ أَشِدَّاءُ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ رُحَمَاءُ بَيْنَهُمْ تَرَاهُمْ رُكَّعًا سُجَّدًا يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوَانًا سِيمَاهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ مِنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ ذَلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ فَآزَرَهُ فَاسْتَغْلَظَ فَاسْتَوَى عَلَى سُوقِهِ يُعْجِبُ الزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ الْكُفَّارَ وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ مِنْهُمْ مَغْفِرَةً وَأَجْرًا عَظِيمًا (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُحَمَّدٌ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject). Regarding the khabar (predicate) there are two views. First: it is «رَسُولُ اللَّهِ», so the pause is complete there — unless you make «الَّذِينَ» genitive, conjoined to the name of Allah, i.e. "and the messenger of those who …"; on this view «أَشِدَّاءُ» means "they are severe".
The second view: «رَسُولُ اللَّهِ» is an adjective (ṣifa), «الَّذِينَ» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the mubtadaʾ, and «أَشِدَّاءُ» is the khabar. And (رُحَمَاءُ) is a second khabar, and likewise «تَرَاهُمْ» and «يَبْتَغُونَ»; «تَرَاهُمْ» may also be resumptive.
(أَشِدَّاءَ) and (رُحَمَاءَ) are also read in the accusative, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative pronoun in the adverb, which is «مَعَهُ». And سُجَّدًا is a second ḥāl, or an anticipated (muqaddara) ḥāl from the pronoun in «رُكَّعًا».
«يَبْتَغُونَ» may also be a third ḥāl.
His saying, Exalted is He: (سِيمَاهُمْ): it is fiʿl [Translator's note: so in the source; probably the pattern فِعْلَى is meant] from سَامَ يَسُومُ, and it means "mark", from His saying, Exalted is He: (مُسَوِّمِينَ). And (فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and «مِنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition phrase.
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ): if you wish, you may conjoin it to the first likeness, i.e. "these are their descriptions in the two Books"; on this view the kāf is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "they are like a crop"; or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "resembling"; or as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a likening like a crop".
And (شَطْأَهُ) with hamza, and without hamza and without alif; its explanation is that he cast the vowel of the hamza onto the ṭāʾ and dropped it. It is also read with alif by substitution, and with a long vowel and hamza, which is a dialect.
And (عَلَى سُوقِهِ) may be a ḥāl, i.e. "standing on its stems", or an adverb (ẓarf).
And (يُعْجِبُ) is a ḥāl. And (مِنْهُمْ) is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins), honouring them by singling them out for mention. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:5-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيُدْخِلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَيُكَفِّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا (٥) وَيُعَذِّبَ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَالْمُشْرِكَاتِ الظَّانِّينَ بِاللَّهِ ظَنَّ السَّوْءِ عَلَيْهِمْ دَائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَعَنَهُمْ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَهَنَّمَ وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْفَوْز, because it was originally an adjective (ṣifa) of it; it was put first and so became a ḥāl. It may also be an adverb (ẓarf) for the place of the triumph, or for what الْفَوْز indicates; but it may not be an adverb for الْفَوْز itself, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). And (الظَّانِّينَ) is an adjective of both groups.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وَتُوَقِّرُوهُ وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِتُؤْمِنُوا): with tāʾ, as an address, because the meaning is "We sent him to you".
And with yāʾ, because what precedes it is in the third person.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Fatḥ
Medinan in its entirety, by consensus
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا فَتَحْنا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُبِينًا﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that it is the opening (fatḥ) of al-Ḥudaybiya, and this opening took place without fighting; it was said that it came about through mutual agreement between the parties. "اَلْحُدَيْبِيَةُ" is a well, and the place was named after the well. Fatḥ (opening, conquest) is simply gaining possession of a place, a city or a town, whether by war or without war, whether it was entry by force or by treaty: it is a fatḥ, because the place is closed, and when it comes into one's hand it is an opening. The meaning of "فَتَحْنا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُبِينًا" — and Allah knows best — is guidance to Islam. It has come in the tafsīr: "We have decreed for you a clear decree", that is: We have judged in your favour with the manifesting of the religion of Islam and victory over your enemy. Most of what has come in the tafsīr is that it is the opening of al-Ḥudaybiya. In the opening of al-Ḥudaybiya there was a great sign among the signs of the Prophet ﷺ: it was a well, and all the water in it was drawn until it was drained and no water remained in it; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rinsed his mouth and spat the water into it, and the well flowed with water until everyone who was with the Prophet ﷺ drank. This does not depart from the meaning of "فَتَحْنا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُبِينًا", namely that by it guidance to Islam is meant. The proof of that is His saying ﴿لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ ما تَقَدَّمَ مِن ذَنْبِكَ وما تَأخَّرَ ويُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ ويَهْدِيَكَ صِراطًا مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 2]. So the meaning is: "We have opened for you an opening in the religion, so that you and the Muslims may be guided by it."

zajjaj:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُبايِعُونَكَ إنَّما يُبايِعُونَ اللَّهَ يَدُ اللَّهِ فَوْقَ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾, that is: your taking the pledge from them is a compact for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, binding upon them. The meaning of ﴿يَدُ اللَّهِ فَوْقَ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾ admits three aspects, two of which have come in the tafsīr (exegesis). One of them: "the hand of Allah in fulfilment is above their hands"; and it has also come: "the hand of Allah in reward is above their hands". And the interpretation — and Allah knows best — is: the hand of Allah in His favour upon them in guidance is above their hands in obedience.
His saying: ﴿فَمَن نَكَثَ فَإنَّما يَنْكُثُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ﴾: "اَلنَّكْثُ" in the language is undoing what you have tied and what you have set right. It has come in the tafsīr: three things recoil upon those who do them; one of them is breaking faith (al-nakth), then wrongdoing (al-baghy) — Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّما بَغْيُكم عَلى أنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ [Yūnus: 23] — and scheming (al-makr) — Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلا يَحِيقُ المَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إلا بِأهْلِهِ﴾ [Fāṭir: 43].
His saying: ﴿فَمَن نَكَثَ فَإنَّما يَنْكُثُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ ومَن أوْفى بِما عاهَدَ عَلَيْهُ اللَّهَ فَسَيُؤْتِيهِ أجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾: it is also read "فَسَنُؤْتِيهِ أجْرًا عَظِيمًا" (We shall give him a great reward), and it is read "عَلَيْهِ اللَّهَ" and "عَلَيْهُ اللَّهَ". We have explained the like of this previously.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
﴿سَيَقُولُ لَكَ المُخَلَّفُونَ مِنَ الأعْرابِ شَغَلَتْنا أمْوالُنا وأهْلُونا فاسْتَغْفِرْ لَنا﴾: with the rāʾ pronounced distinctly before the lām. It has been transmitted from Abū ʿAmr: "فاسْتَغْفِلَّنا", with assimilation (idghām), and likewise in His saying "يَغْفِلَّكُمْ". Sībawayh and al-Khalīl do not permit the assimilation of rāʾ into lām, nor do they report this usage from any of the Arabs. They state that assimilating rāʾ into lām is not permissible, because rāʾ in their view is a repeated (trilled) letter, and if it were assimilated into lām this fullness in it would be lost. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that these people are hypocrites, and said: ﴿يَقُولُونَ بِألْسِنَتِهِمْ ما لَيْسَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that they stayed behind from going out with the Prophet ﷺ because they thought an evil thought, and Allah informed His Prophet of that. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَلْ ظَنَنْتُمْ أنْ لَنْ يَنْقَلِبَ الرَّسُولُ والمُؤْمِنُونَ إلى أهْلِيهِمْ أبَدًا وزُيِّنَ ذَلِكَ في قُلُوبِكم وظَنَنْتُمْ ظَنَّ السَّوْءِ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 12], that is: a thought of corruption, ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا بُورًا﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 12], that is: perishing in the sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, corrupt in His knowledge.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿شَغَلَتْنا أمْوالُنا﴾, that is: we have no one to look after them; ﴿وَأهْلُونا﴾, that is: and our families kept us busy, we have no one to take our place among them. "وَأهْلُنا" is also permissible, but the well-known reading is with the wāw. Whoever says "وَأهْلُونا", it is the plural of "أهْلٌ": "أهْلُونَ"; and whoever says "وَأهْلُنا", it comprises the whole group.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿سَيَقُولُ المُخَلَّفُونَ إذا انْطَلَقْتُمْ إلى مَغانِمَ لِتَأْخُذُوها ذَرُونا نَتَّبِعْكم يُرِيدُونَ أنْ يُبَدِّلُوا كَلامَ اللَّهِ﴾: by His saying ﴿يُرِيدُونَ أنْ يُبَدِّلُوا كَلامَ اللَّهِ﴾ is meant His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقُلْ لَنْ تَخْرُجُوا مَعِيَ أبَدًا ولَنْ تُقاتِلُوا مَعِيَ عَدُوًّا﴾ [al-Tawba: 83]; they wanted to bring about something that would undo this. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that they do not understand and are not able to do that, and said: ﴿قُلْ لَنْ تَتَّبِعُونا كَذَلِكم قالَ اللَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾. Had the speech been a prohibition, He would have said: "قُلْ لا تَتَّبِعُونا" (say: do not follow us). It has been read: "يُرِيدُونَ أنْ يُبَدِّلُوا كَلِمَ اللَّهِ"; al-kalim is the plural of "كَلِمَةٌ", and al-kalām stands in the place of al-taklīm (speaking).

zajjaj:3-3.t: The meaning of ﴿وَيَنْصُرَكَ اللَّهُ نَصْرًا عَزِيزًا﴾ is: a victory possessing might, with which no humiliation occurs. Then He made known the causes of the opening of the religion to His Prophet, upon him be peace, and said: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أنْـزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ في قُلُوبِ المُؤْمِنِينَ لِيَزْدادُوا إيمانًا مَعَ إيمانِهِمْ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 4], that is: He settled in their hearts reverence for Allah and for His Messenger, and composure.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ وكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا﴾: its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is that everything Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are soldiers of His, because all of that shows that He is One, and that no one is able to produce the like of a single thing of what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth. It is also part of the proof that the meaning of His saying ﴿إنّا فَتَحْنا لَكَ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 1] is: We have guided you to Islam and opened for you the matter of the religion.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيُعَذِّبَ المُنافِقِينَ والمُنافِقاتِ والمُشْرِكِينَ والمُشْرِكاتِ الظّانِّينَ بِاللَّهِ ظَنَّ السَّوْءِ عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ﴾: they used to think that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made to seem fair in their hearts; so Allah made the turn of evil fall upon them. Whoever reads "ظَنَّ السُّوءِ", it is likewise as you see. Abū Isḥāq said: I do not know anyone who read it so; and it has also been said that it was read so. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh claimed that the meaning of "اَلسَّوْءُ" here is corruption, and the meaning is: "اَلظّانِّينَ بِاللَّهِ ظَنَّ الفَسادِ" (who think of Allah a thought of corruption), which is their thinking that the Messenger, upon him be peace, and those with him would not return.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ﴾, that is: corruption and destruction fall upon them, ﴿وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ ولَعَنَهم وأعَدَّ لَهم جَهَنَّمَ وساءَتْ مَصِيرًا﴾

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: its explanation is like the first. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا﴾: exalted, wise in what He has arranged.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا أرْسَلْناكَ شاهِدًا ومُبَشِّرًا ونَذِيرًا﴾, that is: a witness over your community on the Day of Resurrection; and this is an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial; ḥāl muqaddara), that is: "a bringer of good tidings of the Garden to whoever does good, and a warner of the Fire to whoever does evil.
[Translator's note: the opening quotation mark in the source is not closed.]

zajjaj:9-9.t:
﴿لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ﴾: the address is to the Prophet ﷺ and an address to the people and to his community, and the meaning indicates that. "لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ" (that they may believe in Allah and His Messenger) is also permissible, and it has been read both ways. It is also possible that "لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ" is an address to the believers and to the Prophet together, because the Prophet ﷺ has believed in Allah, His signs, His books and His messengers.
His saying ﴿شاهِدًا﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 8] is an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial; ḥāl muqaddara), that is: it will be on the Day of Resurrection; while bringing good tidings and warning are a ḥāl in which the Prophet ﷺ was engaged in this world for those of his community who saw him in it, and an anticipated ḥāl for those of his community who come after him until the Day of Resurrection and did not see him. By his word "مُقَدَّرَةً" (anticipated) he means that the ḥāl, in his view, at the time of the report is of two kinds: an accompanying ḥāl, in which the one reported about is engaged at the time of the report, and an anticipated ḥāl, which is estimated to be engaged in at a second point in time.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وتُوَقِّرُوهُ﴾: the meaning of "تُعَزِّرُوهُ" is: you help him. One says "عَزَّرْتُهُ، أُعَزِّرُهُ", that is: I helped him time after time. It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis): "that you help him with the sword". "وَتَعْزُرُوهُ" is also permissible; one says "عَزَرْتُهُ، أعْزُرُهُ، عَزْرًا" and "عَزَّرْتُهُ، أُعَزِّرُهُ، عَزْرًا، وتَعْزِيرًا". Helping the Prophet ﷺ is helping Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. ﴿وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وأصِيلا﴾: this hāʾ refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. The meaning of "يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّهَ" is: they pray to Him. "اَلتَّسْبِيحُ" in the language is magnifying Allah and declaring Him free of evil.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ لِلْمُخَلَّفِينَ مِنَ الأعْرابِ سَتُدْعَوْنَ إلى قَوْمٍ أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ تُقاتِلُونَهم أوْ يُسْلِمُونَ﴾: it has also been read "أوْ يُسْلِمُوا", and the meaning is: "you will fight them until they submit", and "unless they submit.
[Translator's note: the opening quotation mark in the source is not closed.]
If someone says: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: ﴿لَنْ تَخْرُجُوا مَعِيَ أبَدًا ولَنْ تُقاتِلُوا مَعِيَ عَدُوًّا﴾ [al-Tawba: 83], so how could it be permissible for Him to say: ﴿سَتُدْعَوْنَ إلى قَوْمٍ أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ تُقاتِلُونَهم أوْ يُسْلِمُونَ﴾? [The answer is that] he ﷺ said that only because Allah had made known to him that they were hypocrites, and had also made known to him that they would not fight with him. It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that by His saying ﴿سَتُدْعَوْنَ إلى قَوْمٍ أُولِي بَأْسٍ﴾ the Banū Ḥanīfa are meant, whom Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, fought in the days of Musaylima; and it has also come: Hawāzin. The meaning is that it was incumbent on the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ to call everyone whose outward state was Islam to jihad; the Companions were not informed, at the time of jihad, of who would fight and who would not, nor of who was a hypocrite and who was not, because being shown that is one of the signs of the prophets, upon them be peace. It has also been said: ﴿إلى قَوْمٍ أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾, that is: to Persia and Byzantium, and that was in the days of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, Allah's mercy be upon them both, and those after them.
﴿فَإنْ تُطِيعُوا يُؤْتِكُمُ اللَّهُ أجْرًا حَسَنًا﴾, that is: if you repent, abandon hypocrisy and strive, Allah will give you a goodly reward; ﴿وَإنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا كَما تَوَلَّيْتُمْ مِن قَبْلُ يُعَذِّبْكم عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾, that is: if you persist in your hypocrisy and turn away from faith and jihad, as you turned away in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, He will punish you with a painful punishment.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known the report of those whose intention was sincere, and said: ﴿لَقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ المُؤْمِنِينَ إذْ يُبايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ فَعَلِمَ ما في قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, that is: He knew that they were sincere. It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that those who pledged allegiance under the tree (were one thousand four hundred; it was also said: one thousand five hundred; and it was said: one thousand three hundred. They had pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ that they would not turn their backs in fighting nor flee, and it was named "بَيْعَةَ الرِّضْوانِ" (the Pledge of Good Pleasure) because of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لَقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ المُؤْمِنِينَ إذْ يُبايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾. The tree was a samura (acacia). ﴿فَأنْـزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وأثابَهم فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا﴾: it was said that it is the conquest of Khaybar; ﴿وَمَغانِمَ كَثِيرَةً يَأْخُذُونَها وكانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 19]
[Translator's note: the opening parenthesis in the source is not closed.]

zajjaj:20-20.t: ﴿وَعَدَكُمُ اللَّهُ مَغانِمَ كَثِيرَةً تَأْخُذُونَها فَعَجَّلَ لَكم هَذِهِ﴾: this repetition is a repetition in the promise, that is: He hastened this, meaning Khaybar. ﴿وَكَفَّ أيْدِيَ النّاسِ عَنْكم ولِتَكُونَ آيَةً لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, that is: He restrained the hands of the people from you when they went out and left their dependants behind in Medina; Allah protected their dependants and their home territory, when the Jews had intended [harm] against them, and Allah prevented them from that.

zajjaj:21-21.t: ﴿وَأُخْرى لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْها قَدْ أحاطَ اللَّهُ بِها﴾: the meaning is: Allah has promised you other spoils which Allah has encompassed — Allah has known them — and that is what the Muslims will take as spoil, up to the point that no one fights them.

zajjaj:22-22.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ قاتَلَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوَلَّوُا الأدْبارَ ثُمَّ لا يَجِدُونَ ولِيًّا ولا نَصِيرًا﴾ ﴿سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 23]: the meaning is: had those who did not fight you fought you, you would have been given victory over them, because the way (sunna) of Allah is victory for His allies and His party; ﴿وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلا﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 23]. "سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ" is accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because His saying ﴿لَوَلَّوُا الأدْبارَ﴾ means: "Allah has ordained their abandonment as a way". The like of this has already passed in His saying ﴿كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 24] and in His saying ﴿صُنْعَ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Naml: 88]. Had it been read "سُنَّةُ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلُ" (nominative), it would have been good in Arabic, the meaning being: "That is the way of Allah which has passed before"; but I do not know anyone who read it so, so do not read it so.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي كَفَّ أيْدِيَهم عَنْكم وأيْدِيَكم عَنْهم بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ﴾: "مَكَّةَ" is a diptote (does not take tanwīn), because it is feminine and it is definite.
His saying: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ أنْ أظْفَرَكم عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) «that twelve men were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who had been taken without covenant or compact, and the Prophet ﷺ let them go and showed them grace»; and the outcome of that was that a man's relatives and whoever was a believer were kept safe from being harmed. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْلا رِجالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ ونِساءٌ مُؤْمِناتٌ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهم أنْ تَطَئُوهم فَتُصِيبَكم مِنهم مَعَرَّةٌ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 25]. The position of "أنْ" is nominative, a badal (substitute) for "رِجالٌ"; the meaning is: "were it not that you would trample believing men and believing women". Then He said: ﴿لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا لَعَذَّبْنا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنهم عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 25], that is: had the disbelievers been separated from the Muslims, We would have sent down upon the disbelievers what would be a punishment for them in this world. As for the meaning of ﴿فَتُصِيبَكم مِنهم مَعَرَّةٌ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 25], it was said: "were it not that you would kill some believing people among them by mistake, so that blood-money would be due from you"; and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "were it not for the aversion to hardship befalling you by killing those who are of your religion, since you are mixed with them, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment."

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿هُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوكم عَنِ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ والهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفًا أنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ﴾: "اَلْهَدْيَ" is accusative (manṣūb), coordinated (nasaq) with the kāf and mīm; the meaning is: "and they turned away the sacrificial animals". "مَعْكُوفًا": detained from reaching its place of sacrifice. ﴿وَلَوْلا رِجالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, as we have described, We would have given you victory over them; but what prevented that was the aversion to trampling the believers with harm and killing. The position of "أنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ" is accusative, in the sense of: "and they turned away the sacrificial animals, detained from reaching their place of sacrifice."

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ وعَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: Allah sent down upon them composure and dignity. ﴿وَألْزَمَهم كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوى﴾: it has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that their watchword was "لا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ" (there is no god but Allah); and the word of God-fearing is affirming the oneness of Allah and believing in His Messenger, upon him be peace. ﴿وَكانُوا أحَقَّ بِها وأهْلَها﴾, that is: they were more entitled to it than others, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, chose for His Prophet ﷺ and for His religion the people of goodness, those deserving of it, and those more fitting for guidance than others.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيا بِالحَقِّ لَتَدْخُلُنَّ المَسْجِدَ الحَرامَ إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكم ومُقَصِّرِينَ لا تَخافُونَ﴾: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw in his sleep as though he and his Companions, may Allah have mercy on them, were entering Mecca with heads shaved and hair cut short. So Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision, and they entered as he had seen; they had thought the entry slow in coming. The meaning of ﴿إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ comes out in two ways. One of them: "if Allah commands you to it". And it is possible — and it is good — that "إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ" runs according to what Allah has commanded concerning everything that is expected to be done, for He said: ﴿وَلا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إنِّي فاعِلٌ ذَلِكَ غَدًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 23] ﴿إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Kahf: 24]

zajjaj:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ والَّذِينَ مَعَهُ أشِدّاءُ عَلى الكُفّارِ رُحَماءُ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: Allah described them as being tender toward one another, that upon them are composure and dignity, that they are sincere in affection toward one another, and that they are severe against the disbelievers. "أشِدّاءُ" is the plural of "شَدِيدٌ"; the original is "أشْدِداءُ", like "نَصِيبٌ" and "أنْصِباءُ", but the two dāls were both voweled, so the first was assimilated into the second. Like this is His saying: ﴿مَن يَرْتَدَّ مِنكم عَنْ دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهم ويُحِبُّونَهُ أذِلَّةٍ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ أعِزَّةٍ عَلى الكافِرِينَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 54]. And His saying: ﴿سِيماهم في وُجُوهِهِمْ مِن أثَرِ السُّجُودِ﴾, that is: on their faces is the mark of prostration, which is the mark of those humble before Allah who pray. It was also said: they will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with shining foreheads, hands and feet from the traces of ablution; Allah will make this a mark for them on the Day of Resurrection, and it is the sīmāʾ (mark), by which He shows their superiority over others.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ مَثَلُهم في التَّوْراةِ ومَثَلُهم في الإنْجِيلِ﴾, that is: that is the description of Muḥammad ﷺ and his Companions in the Torah. Then He made known that their description in the Gospel is also: ﴿كَزَرْعٍ أخْرَجَ شَطْأهُ فَآزَرَهُ فاسْتَغْلَظَ فاسْتَوى عَلى سُوقِهِ﴾. The meaning of "أخْرَجَ شَطْأهُ" is: it put forth its shoots. ﴿فَآزَرَهُ فاسْتَغْلَظَ﴾, that is: the large ones supported the small ones until they became level with one another. ﴿عَلى سُوقِهِ﴾: plural of "ساقٌ" (stalk).
His saying: ﴿يُعْجِبُ الزُّرّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ الكُفّارَ﴾: "اَلزُّرّاعُ" (the sowers) are Muḥammad, upon him be peace, and those who call to Islam, namely his Companions.
His saying: ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ مِنهم مَغْفِرَةً وأجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾: concerning "مِنهُمْ" there are two views. [The first is] that "مِنهُمْ" here sets the genus apart from what is other than it, as you say: "أنْفِقْ نَفَقَتَكَ مِنَ الدَّراهِمِ، لا مِنَ الدَّنانِيرِ" (spend your expenditure from dirhams, not from dinars), the meaning being: "make your expenditure of this kind"; and as He said: ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأوْثانِ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 30] — He does not mean that some of them are filth and some are not filth; rather the meaning is: "avoid the filth which is the idols". So the meaning is: "Allah has promised those of the believing Companions of the Prophet ﷺ who believed and did righteous deeds a great reward, and Allah has preferred them over others for their precedence and the greatness of their reward. The second aspect is that the meaning is: "Allah has promised those of them who persevered in faith and righteous action forgiveness and a great reward.
